title: Linux systemd conflict - help requested
body:
We recently resolved - #4105 - a problem where a systemd configuration entry (PrivateTmp=true) was found to be the culprit in making idle detection fail.

I'm now encountering a different problem, which appears to require that we set PrivateTmp=true again, to work round a different problem. Obviously these two needs are incompatible.

The new problem arises at GPUGrid, where they are beta-testing a new app which requires the Wrapper app to perform a software installation. The wrapper command is
```
    <task>
        <application>/usr/bin/flock</application>
	<command_line>$PROJECT_DIR/miniconda.lock -c "/bin/bash ./miniconda-installer.sh -b -u -p $PROJECT_DIR/miniconda &&
                      $PROJECT_DIR/miniconda/bin/conda install -m -y -p gpugridpy --file requirements.txt "
	</command_line>
	<setenv>PATH=/usr/bin:/bin</setenv>
	<time_limit>1800</time_limit>
	<weight>10</weight>
    </task>
```
If `PrivateTmp=false` (the new default), this command fails with
```
21:48:18 (21729): wrapper: running /usr/bin/flock (/var/lib/boinc-client/projects/www.gpugrid.net/miniconda.lock -c "/bin/bash ./miniconda-installer.sh -b -u -p /var/lib/boinc-client/projects/www.gpugrid.net/miniconda &&
                      /var/lib/boinc-client/projects/www.gpugrid.net/miniconda/bin/conda install -m -y -p gpugridpy --file requirements.txt ")
[21755] INTERNAL ERROR: cannot create temporary directory!
[21759] INTERNAL ERROR: cannot create temporary directory!
21:48:19 (21729): /usr/bin/flock exited; CPU time 0.118700
21:48:19 (21729): app exit status: 0x1
21:48:19 (21729): called boinc_finish(195)
```
If `PrivateTmp=true`, the wrapper task succeeds, and the full BOINC job carries on to a successful conclusion.

Could the systemd crew - @BryanQuigley, @Germano0, @smoe - please put their thinking caps on and suggest how this might be resolved? I'm assuming that the basic problem in the 'false' case is that the system /tmp/ structure is read-only to BOINC?

https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/systemd.exec.5.html has details which may be relevant:

>        PrivateTmp=
           Takes a boolean argument. If true, sets up a new file system
           namespace for the executed processes and mounts private /tmp/ and
           /var/tmp/ directories inside it that are not shared by processes
           outside of the namespace. This is useful to secure access to
           temporary files of the process, but makes sharing between
           processes via /tmp/ or /var/tmp/ impossible.

title: client: only report a graphics app if file is there can we can execute it
body:
Problem: when parsing an APP_VERSIOn (e.g. in scheduler reply)
we check whether it has a graphics app (i.e. a file named "graphics_app").
If so we could report it to the GUI before the file has been downloaded,
causing an error when "Shot Graphics" is clicked.

Also, on Mac we check whether the graphics app can run on
this CPU, given its header.
But this check was being done during APP_VERSION parsing,
when typically the file doesn't exist yet.

Fix: when parsing APP_VERSION,
store a pointer to the FILE_INFO for the graphics app.
When reporting an ACTIVE_TASK to the GUI,
check whether the file is present and (on Mac) can be executed.
Only then tell the GUI about it.
If the file download failed or the file can't be executed,
zero out the pointer so we don't do the check again.

title: Server: Bug: Runtime of MT tasks underestimated in sched_send
body:
**Describe the bug**
When a client requests work, the request is expressed in core-seconds. The server doesn't factor in the core usage.

**Expected behavior**
The server needs to estimate the real cpu usage, across all applicable cores, for MT tasks.

**Log entries**
```
14/01/2021 19:30:21 |  | [work_fetch] Request work fetch: project work fetch resumed by user
14/01/2021 19:30:22 |  | [work_fetch] target work buffer: 8640.00 + 864.00 sec
14/01/2021 19:30:22 |  | [work_fetch] shortfall 38016.00 nidle 4.00 saturated 0.00 busy 0.00
14/01/2021 19:30:22 | Milkyway@Home | [sched_op] CPU work request: 38016.00 seconds; 4.00 devices
14/01/2021 19:30:24 | Milkyway@Home | Scheduler request completed: got 23 new tasks
14/01/2021 19:30:24 | Milkyway@Home | [sched_op] estimated total CPU task duration: 39233 seconds
```
```
11/01/2021 12:00:39 | PrimeGrid | CPU needs work - buffer low
11/01/2021 12:00:39 | PrimeGrid | [work_fetch] request: CPU (38016.00 sec, 4.00 inst) Intel GPU (0.00 sec, 0.00 inst)
11/01/2021 12:00:39 | PrimeGrid | [sched_op] CPU work request: 38016.00 seconds; 4.00 devices
11/01/2021 12:00:40 | PrimeGrid | Scheduler request completed: got 48 new tasks
11/01/2021 12:00:40 | PrimeGrid | [sched_op] estimated total CPU task duration: 56610 seconds
```
In both cases, the 'target work buffer' is expressed in wall time - 9,504 seconds, or about 2 hours 40 minutes.
But the 'request' is for four times that much - over 10 hours of core-time.
In both these cases, the scheduler went on adding MT tasks to the reply **as if single threaded** until the work request was fulfilled. Work for **over ten hours of wall-time** was delivered (more for PrimeGrid, which still uses DCF).

The server estimates task duration at
https://github.com/BOINC/boinc/blob/master/sched/sched_send.cpp#L429 (estimate_duration_unscaled) and
https://github.com/BOINC/boinc/blob/master/sched/sched_send.cpp#L477 (estimate_duration)
Neither routine considers the core loading of the MT tasks allocated.

avg_ncpus is available in the HOST_USAGE structure, and should be considered in either `estimate_duration_unscaled` or `estimate_duration`.

title: Improve the out-of-box experience for scientists
body:
Suppose a scientist (let’s call her Mary) needs lots of high-throughput computing and can’t afford the usual sources.  Let’s assume that

- Mary’s programs are Linux/Intel executables or Python scripts.  She normally runs them on a Linux laptop.
- Mary has access to a Linux server on the Internet.  She doesn’t necessarily have root access, but can ask a sysadmin to install packages.
- Mary knows Linux as a user, but not Docker, databases, web servers, AWS,  etc.

Mary hears about volunteer computing and BOINC, and decides to investigate it.  Mary will use BOINC only if this initial “out-of-box experience” (OOBE) is positive; i.e. she quickly tries out BOINC and is convinced that it works, that it’s useful to her, and that she wants to use it going forward.  The ideal scenario is something like:

- Mary hears about BOINC and goes to the web site.
- Within ~1 hour she successfully runs jobs, using existing applications, on ~100 volunteer computers.
- What she ends up with is something that she can continue to use in production, and to which she can add other applications, GPU apps, larger volumes of jobs and data, BOINC features like result validation, etc.

The current BOINC OOBE doesn’t achieve this.  The main BOINC server documentation (https://boinc.berkeley.edu/trac/wiki/ProjectMain) is a sprawling mess.  Marius’ Docker work (https://github.com/marius311/boinc-server-docker/blob/master/docs/cookbook.md) is a big step in the right direction, but more is needed to complete the above scenario.

BOINC competes with systems like HTCondor and AWS.  We should study the OOBEs of these systems, borrow their good ideas, and make sure that we’re competitive. See, for example, https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCd1UBXmZIgB4p85t2tu-gLw

## The goal
The following is a sketch of what I think the OOBE should be like.  The target configuration involves:

- A “server host”.  This runs a BOINC server, as a set of Docker containers.  It must be on a machine visible to the outside Internet, possibly a cloud instance.
- One or more “job submission hosts”.  Scientists log in to these to do their work.  They may be behind a firewall.

### Setting up the server host

This involves downloading a .gz file containing the BOINC server software and some VM and docker images.  Then you run a script that asks one or two questions, then creates and runs a server (as Docker processes).  It creates a read-me file saying:

- How to make the server start on boot (edit /etc files).
- Where the config files are in case you need to change something later.

Admin functions (start/stop server, create accounts for job submitters) are done through a web interface.  After the initial setup there should be no need to log in.

### Setting up a job submission host
This involves installing a package that contains job submission scripts (see below) but not the BOINC server.
### Running jobs
We should handle at least two cases:

- The scientist has an executable and the libraries it needs.
- The scientist has a Python script and the modules it needs.

In each case, let’s assume that all files for an app are stored in a directory.

To submit a job:

boinc_run --app app_dir_path

Run this in a directory containing input files.  It makes a job with those input files, running the given app. The file “cmdline”, if present, contains command-line args.

To run multiple jobs, create a directory for each job, and put input files there.  Then do

boinc_run_jobs --app app_dir_path dir1 dir2 ...

To see the status of the job(s) started in the current directory:

boinc_status 

If the job failed, show info like stderr output.

To abort jobs started in the current directory.

boinc_abort

To fetch the output files of completed jobs started in the current directory.

boinc_fetch

Note: fancier features can be added to this, but the basic features are ultra-simple.  No XML editing, estimating job sizes, etc.
## Implementation
The implementation shouldn’t be that hard.  It’s based on technology we already have: boinc-server-docker and boinc2docker, and the remote job and file management mechanisms.

The server host setup script creates a BOINC project running in Docker containers, equipped with the VBox-based universal app, and some standard Docker containers, e.g. for Python apps.

On the submission host, each user has a directory ~/.boinc to contain various configuration and status files.  A file ~/.boinc/apps contains a list of applications that have been used.  Each one is identified by a directory path. We keep track of the mod time of the directory and the files in it; we maintain a Docker layer corresponding to the application.

The boinc_run command (a Python script) does the following:

- Check ~/.boinc/apps to see whether we have a Docker layer for the app.  If not, build one using boinc2docker.
- Use the remote file management mechanism to copy files (app and input) to the Apache container.
- Use the remote job submission mechanism to submit the job.  Write its ID to a file.

boinc_status etc. use the remote job submission mechanism.

## Computing resources

The scientist starts by running the BOINC client on one or more of their own computers (possibly Windows or Mac), and attaching to the project.

When things are working and they’re ready to scale up, they register with Science United, supplying their keywords.  The vetting process may take a day or two.  This will typically provide them with several hundred hosts.

Another possibility is to allow Science United users to register as “testers”, and to add a mechanism where projects can register as “test projects” on SU, with no vetting.  Such projects would be allowed only to use VM apps with no network access (we’d need to add a mechanism for this).  They’d get some number of hosts (50-100) for a few days.

## Restructuring server documentation

Once we have this working, we need to reorganize the server docs in such a way that scientists are initially steered toward the OOBE described here, but can still access lower-level info.

title: GPUs are underutilized
body:
I dedicated a few NVidia Quadro K6000 GPUs to various projects. These GPUs are older but they are still monsters in GFLOPs performance with over 2800 compute cores. The newer boards have even more. In other words, the GPU pipeline can easily handle several kernels simultaneously. But, I barely see 15-20% GPU load on a single GPU task. Basically, the compute kernels launched do not have enough numeric complexity. I see the projects like Milkyway@home and Universe@home running GPU tasks for 3-5 minutes. 

What needs to happen is a better load balancer to launch more than one task per GPU. The current design will result in increasingly less resource utilization (or underutilization) as the hardware is becoming more and more powerful. 

I believe all NVidia and AMD compute cards report the computational load and memory utilization. Therefore, Boinc manager can launch automatically as well. But, it may be better to communicate with the user code about the resource needs. Therefore, the user code should be able to notify Boinc manager about the compute cores it will be taking for GPU tasks and additional tasks should be allowed by the Boinc manager up to total compute cores. 

In the short run, Boinc manager can readily start multiple GPU tasks on a single GPU and check the load on the GPU. In the long run, the user code should supply hints about the maximum load it will use in advance. 

Just a thought.

title: Maximum CPU time - spread tasks evenly over timeslot
body:
**Describe the problem**
When choosing a value of 'Maximum % of CPU time" BOINC will schedule the runtime in seconds.
For example, selecting 25% will make BOINC tasks run for one second, and sleep for 3 seconds.
In a multi core environment this is quite detrimental for performance, power spikes and more.
Also when all the tasks start at once, the computer often is less responsive for one second, and then 3 seconds is very usable.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
It would be beneficial for the system to spread the multi-core tasks in time, using slots.
For example, if we have an 8 core system with a 25% usage selected, we have have 8 tasks running:
- First second: run 2 tasks out of the 8 (tasks 1, 2)
- Second second: run next 2 tasks out of the 8 (task 3, 4)
- Third second: run other 2 tasks (task 5, 6)
- Fourth second: run other 2 tasks (tasks 7,8)

Second example:
In a 100 core system with a 1% CPU load selected:
In the old situation all 100 cores would run for 1 second, completely bogging down the system.
For the next 99 seconds there would be no BOINC tasks running.
In the new situation, every task would run for 1 second in consecutive order.

This would provide a better user experience:
- Fans will not throttle up and down that aggressively reducing noise
- Power supplies have a less hard time
- More gentle thermal effect on CPU (less expansion/contraction cycles
- Computer is more usable in general
- Simply makes much more sense

**Additional context**
In case you want your computer to consume a steady amount of power this is the only way.

Note: It would be beneficial that CPU % LOAD is separately configurable to GPU % LOAD. Same concept, but time slots also take into account amount of GPUs installed in the system.

title: Make lock files inheritable in Python >= 3.4
body:
Fixes # N/A

**Description of the Change**
In `sched/start`, a lock is obtained for each of the daemon processes by creating a lockfile and locking it with `fcntl.lockf()`.  If the lock succeeds, the daemon process is later spawned using `os.execvp()`.  However -- per [Python's documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#inheritance-of-file-descriptors) -- "[s]ince Python 3.4, file descriptors created by Python are non-inheritable by default."  Ergo, the handle to the lockfile is closed upon calling `os.execvp()` and the lock is lost.  This results in the daemons being respawned each time `start` is run.

Python 3.4 introduced a new method in the `os` module called `set_inheritable`.  To fix this issue, we check to see that this function exists (to preserve backwards compatibility); if it exists, we call it to mark the lockfile as inheritable.  That way, the file handle (and its associated lock) are preserved upon calling `os.execvp()`.

**Alternate Designs**
N/A

**Release Notes**
N/A

body: **Describe the bug** The `get_notices` and `get_notices_public` RPC functions may return invalid XML when attributes contain special characters which are not getting properly escaped. Client: App max_concurrent causes continuous work fetch and too many tasks
body:
**Describe the bug**
Continuous work fetch going way past the configured number of days of work. This happens when using app max_concurrent, an amount less then the number of tasks received for this app, and the tasks for this app is the oldest and/or have longest run time. Probably an issue with rr_simulation.

**Steps To Reproduce**
1. Join/run one project website with multiple available apps. (World Community Grid)
2. BOINC settings, store 0 days, store up to 0.2 additional days.
3. Website settings, limit task to one app. (Africa Rainfull Project / ARP1). In World community grid, go to Settings, Device manager, profile, and also increase the project/app limit to 16 or higher or unlimited.
4. After 2 or more tasks are gotten for the same app, switch to another app using website settings.
5. Use app_config.xml, limit max_concurrent on arp1 to 1, or less then the number of arp1 tasks in the BOINC client.

**Expected behavior**
Limit tasks with no work fetch when enough of other apps are in BOINC client.

**System Information**
 - OS: Windows 10
 - BOINC Version: 7.16.11

**Additional context**
Log shows something for rr_simulation, with max_concurrent=12 on Ryzen 3900x 12 core 24 threads. The rr_simulation stops after only 12 ARP1 and fails to see 400 MCM1 tasks. This causes work fetch to keep fetching more new tasks every 2 minutes non-stop, way past the configured configured number of days of work. All 24 threads are fully used with 12 ARP1 plus 12 MCM1/MIP1.

Some log: [boinc_max_concurrent12.txt](https://github.com/BOINC/boinc/files/6295109/boinc_max_concurrent12.txt)

Non-BOINC CPU usage time is incorrect
body:
BOINC's calculation of non-BOINC CPU usage time is incorrect, as processes which exited within the sample interval (typically 10 seconds) are not taken into consideration. This leads to BOINC underestimating the non-BOINC CPU usage, especially in situations where a lot of short-lived processes are present.

We run BOINC as SCHED_IDLE batch process on our Continuous-Integration (CI) nodes and configured BOINC to suspend once more than 10% CPU time is consumed by other applications. But since short-lived processes are very common when compiling (C/C++) projects, BOINC is constantly underestimating the non-BOINC CPU usage. As result, it often kicks in, while a CI jobs is actually fully utilizing the system. Needles to say, that this behavior is undesirable.

I saw that this shortcoming was already identified in https://github.com/BOINC/boinc/pull/3939. But this PR seems to be stalled. Hence, besides this issue acting as tracking issue for the deficiency, please feel encouraged to continue work on PR #3939 by it. :)

title: client: be conservative about non-BOINC CPU usage on underflow
body:
Instead of assume that the non-BOINC CPU usage was 0%, assume that it
was 50%. This potentially prevents BOINC from kicking-in in the
presence of short-lived processes (if configured to run only if
non-BOINC CPU usage is below 50%).

The main issue is that BOINC's calculation of non-BOINC CPU usage time
is incorrect, as processes which exited within the sample
interval (typically 10 seconds) are not taken into consideration. This
leads to BOINC underestimating the non-BOINC CPU usage, especially in
situations where a lot of short-lived processes are present. This
commit does not fix that, but mitigates the effects of this. For more
information, see issue #4327.

client: add a cooldown period before resuming operations
body:
Add a cooldown period, currently 30 seconds, before resuming
operations to prevent frequent running/suspended switches.

BOINCs non-BOINC CPU usage determination is often incorrect (see issue
core machine which compiles LLVM while BOINC is running. BOINC is
configured to suspend computation once non-BOINC CPU usage exceeds
10%. As you can see BOINC frequently reports 0.00% CPU usage. This is
due issue #4327. A workaround is suggested in pull request #4328. This
would change the incorrectly reported value from 0% to 50% non-BOINC
CPU usage. However there are still times where a non-BOINC CPU usage
below 10% is reported. At those times, BOINC would resume its
operation. However in the next cycle, the non-BOINC CPU usage exceeds
10% again. To avoid frequent running/suspended switches of BOINC, this
adds a cooldown period of 30 seconds before BOINC resumes computation.

A logical next step would be to make this cooldown period
configurable, including an option to completely disable the cooldown
period (to restore the original behavior).

title: Authenticate data from the BOINC web site
body:
Currently the BOINC client periodically gets the project list from the BOINC web site.  The data is not authenticated, so a hacker could break into the BOINC web site and distribute a list of bogus projects.

Proposal: Sign the project list and other data, similarly to code-signing.

Create a PKE key pair for the BOINC web site.  The public key is compiled into the BOINC client (or read from a config file?).  The private key is kept on an off-line signing machine.  The project list is signed (off-line) and sent with this signature.

Modify the client to verify the signature.

Notes:

1. Currently, signing is based on MD5 hashes, which have vulnerabilities.  This new mechanism will use a better hash function (say, SHA256).  In theory we could change code-signing to use this also, but that would be a big disruptive change.
2. This mechanism will also be used to authenticate other info exported by the BOINC web site, including BOINC app library info.
3. The project list could include the code-signing key for each project; that would plug an existing security hole.
4. In theory we should have a mechanism for periodically changing the key pair.  In practice I don't think we need to.
5. The client also fetches info on new client versions from the BOINC web site.  This could be signed as well, though I'm not sure it matters.
6. There's a client option for fetching the project list from a different URL.  If this is used, no authentication will be done.
7. This mechanism could be generalized so that the client has a list of (URL, public key) pairs.  Maybe later.

title: Implement a BOINC app library
body:
Maintain a set of commonly-used science applications (Autodock, Charm, LAMMPS, etc.).  For each app, maintain a set of app versions for various platforms and GPUs.  The app versions either

1. are compiled with the BOINC API (preferred)
2. use the BOINC wrapper
3. are VM-based

If the app has a checkpoint mechanism, integrate with BOINC's API.

The app versions must be "safe" in the sense that running the program with arbitrary (possibly malicious) input files and cmdline parameters will not

- access files outside the slot directory (i.e. no absolute paths can be specified on the cmdline)
- use resources in a way that would interfere with system performance (e.g. no fork() bombs).
- do anything else bad.

Each app version can have a plan class, with a corresponding XML plan class specification.

The BOINC web site will serve all the app version files, and will export a signed XML document describing the apps, app versions, and files.  This document is downloaded periodically by the BOINC client.

A BOINC project can use apps from the BOINC library, and serve the files itself.  To do so:

- copy the corresponding directory tree from the BOINC web site (includes app version files and signatures)
- run update_versions

The project doesn't have to code-sign the files.

This sets a "from library" flag in the app XML descriptor, telling the client the app version is from the app library, in which case it:

- checks that the project's app version files match the app library
- authenticates the files with the BOINC signing key

rather than the project signing key.

The app XML descriptor also has a timestamp, which is the update time of the app library when app was copied.  If this is later than client's copy of app library info, the client refreshes the app library info.

Notes:

1. If multiple projects use the same library app, the client will download and store separate copies per project.  It would be possible to change things so that clients get files directly from the app library, and they're shared between projects.  This would be a fairly large change; it would involve server code as well as client.  Maybe later.
2. There will be changes to the app source code to use the BOINC API.  If possible, add these changes (#ifdef'd) to the app's repo.

body:
**Describe the bug**
PrimeGrid and other projects where being "first" with a result is important used zero resource share and zero cache to avoid ANY prefetch of tasks before the current one was completed. fix #2837 changed the test from "idle instance" to "three minutes work remaining". This is a good change for MOST people but broke the special-use case for some.

**Steps To Reproduce**
1. Set resource share on your only project to zero
2. Set cache to 0 days and 'extra' to 0 days

**Expected behavior**
A single task should download and execute. When it completes - and not before! - another task should be downloaded.

**Additional context**
Suggested fix: in work_fetch.cpp line 115 replace

`if (p->resource_share == 0 && rwf.saturated_time > WF_EST_FETCH_TIME) {
     return RSC_REASON_ZERO_SHARE;`

with

`if (p->resource_share == 0 && rwf.saturated_time > WF_EST_FETCH_TIME && gstate.work_buf_min() > WF_EST_FETCH_TIME) {
             return RSC_REASON_ZERO_SHARE;`

This would in addition to zero resource share, check for the zero cache setting. I have NOT been able to test this fix (although it compiles clean), and am not familiar with the internals (are both values in seconds?), so someone much more knowledgeable than I should verify that this will work and not break a hundred other things.

title: [WIP] Mac trigger "Install Rosetta 2?" dialog on Apple Silicon Macs
body:
Apple Silicon (arm64) Macs can run X86_64 executables using Apple's Rosetta 2 x86_64 translation / emulation software. For BOINC projects to take advantage of this, the BOINC client must report the emulated x86_64 CPU features to project servers. The BOINC client launches its detect_rosetta_cpu helper app to determine these features so the client can report them. 

But Rosetta 2 is not installed by default on Apple Silicon Macs. MacOS automatically displays its built-in "Install Rosetta 2?" dialog when a user launches an x86_64-only application if Rosetta 2 has not yet been installed. But detect_rosetta_cpu, which is a bare (command-line) executable rather than a full MacOS application, apparently does not trigger this dialog.

This PR is intended to update the detect_rosetta_cpu helper app to trigger the dialog when appropriate, by embedding an info.plist section in it. We hope that is sufficient to trigger the dialog. If not, we may need to convert the detect_rosetta_cpu command-line executable into a full Mac application bundle.

title: Possibly revise Git Development Workflow and Client Release Procedure for BOINC
body:
This is a continuation of a discussion begun under PR #4267, starting [about here](https://github.com/BOINC/boinc/issues/4267#issuecomment-864531030). We agreed that BOINC's current [GIT development workflow](https://github.com/BOINC/boinc-policy/blob/master/Development_Documents/Development_Workflow.md) and [Client Release Process](https://github.com/BOINC/boinc-policy/blob/master/Development_Documents/Client_Release_Process.md) need review and possibly revision.

In particular, @AenBleidd wrote:
> I think, this development process should be revisited, and I would like to initiate this process. Personally I like the idea of stable and releasable master: it's way more easier and important to test every feature implementation and bug fix than handle hundreds of cherry-picks.

**This is the current development workflow:**

Development is done in Git Master. Developers typically create a new feature branch off master and write their new code in that feature branch. The new code is then tested by the author and possibly by a few others, and then merged into master.

Each release has three numbers: like 7.16.35. In this example, 7 is the _major release number_ and 16 is the _minor release number_. 35 is the _revision number_ (also called the _bug fix number_.) A new release changes the _minor release number_ and occasionally the _major number_. For those, you create a new release branch off master.

A new _revision_ includes only bug fixes to that _major_ and _minor_ release version. For a new _revision_, you cherry-pick only bug fixes from master into the release branch from master. Specifically, the bug fix process is: the developer creates a new bug fix branch, writes and tests the code in that bug fix branch, then merges it into master. Finally, the developer cherry-picks that merge into master.

After the release branch is considered sufficiently stable for wider testing, a test build is made available to our volunteer alpha testers as a  _development version_. If they report bugs, the developers work to fix the bugs, increase the _revision number_ / _bug fix number_, and release it to the alpha testers as a new _development version_. This process repeats until the alpha testers report no new bugs, at which time the _development version_ is released to the general public as the _recommended version_.

If additional bugs are reported by end users, the bug fix process is repeated, with or without further alpha testing, and a new _recommended version_ is released to the public.

**Development workflow proposed by @AenBleidd :** 

In [this comment](https://github.com/BOINC/boinc/issues/4267#issuecomment-864659844), @AenBleidd suggested the following work flow:
> This is an explanation of what I suggest but with two changes:
> 
> their master -> our release
> their develop -> our master

![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3234209/122695424-984f3600-d240-11eb-84b7-eb9fb22db9b6.png)
which I believe was based on [this article](https://yakiloo.com/getting-started-git-flow/).

title: --remote_file parameter in create_work does not seem to work as advertised in documentation
body:
According to [JobSubmission](https://boinc.berkeley.edu/trac/wiki/JobSubmission), we can use the --remote_file parameter to specify a URL, size of the file in bytes, and MD5sum for files served by a separate web server.

Additionally, [JobTemplates](https://boinc.berkeley.edu/trac/wiki/JobTemplates) suggests that there are two ways that we can provide remote file information. Either via parameters in create_work or with input templates. 

The documentation seems to suggest that this is an OR situation, not that we need both. 

Unfortunately, my findings have been that the code path is guaranteed to launch process_input_template, and it will throw an ERR_XML_PARSE if the number of files passed into create_work doesn't equal the number of files given in the wu template.

Ideally we'd like to give create_work the remote_file URL without needing to create an input template for every job, as we have about 1.3 million jobs to create and it seems needlessly messy to create/generate such a large number of templates.

I'm hoping to get some clarification on what the functionality should be., or what I might be doing wrong.

Below is the method by which I'm calling create_work:

```
counter = 0
 while read line; do
  wu_name="appname_$((counter))_$((counter+1))')"
  echo "create_work: ${wu_name}"
  bin/create_work --appname appname \
    --result_template templates/appname_out \
    --remote_file "<URL> 2400 $(echo $line)"\
    --priority 12000 \
    --min_quorum 2 \
    --wu_name "${wu_name}" \
    --rsc_fpops_est 3e13 \
    --rsc_fpops_bound 3e20 \
    --delay_bound 604800
  counter+=1
 done <<< "$(cat ./appname_taskinfo.txt)";
```


Thanks in advance!

title: Ability to "no new tasks" specific application instead of entire project
body:
**Describe the problem**
BOINC currently has a feature where one can set a project as "no new tasks" on a per-client basis which can override settings from an account manager. Some projects offer applications with vastly different computing requirements (GPU vs CPU*), computing time, and efficiency. And some projects may have applications that don't work well across all platforms. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
The ability to mark a specific application (or application version) as "no new tasks" and not request WUs (or reject WUs) for this application. This way, even if a specific application fails often on your system or you simply want to crunch using the most efficient application, you can.

**Additional context**
AFAIK currently the only way to select which applications you want to run is by changing the settings on the project's website, assigning hosts into different groups (home, work, etc). But this can cause problems when using an account manager, and it would be nice to have a local override regardless.

*I am aware that BOINC only downloads applications which there is support for ie it will not download a GPU application if no GPU is installed, but you can't set it to only download GPU applications from a particular project, for example.

[WIP] Auto update certificate bundles
body:
Fixes #4544

**Description of the Change**
Adds code to the BOINC client to automatically download a fresh _ca-bundle.crt_ file from the BOINC server every 2 weeks. It expects the file to be at
`https://boinc.berkeley.edu/ca-bundle.crt` which is a shortcut for the full URL: 
`https://boinc.berkeley.edu/dl/ca-bundle.crt`

**Note**: Currently, this code will not affect curl on MS Windows computers because as of PR #4545 curl uses _schannel_ instead of _openssl_ and so uses the Windows certificate store rather than _curl/ca-bundle.crt_. If it is desired to return to using _curl/ca-bundle.crt_, this automatic updating can be enabled for MS Windows by changing line 55 of _client/http_curl.cpp_ from 
`#define AUTO_UPDATE_MSW_CERTS 0`
 to 
`#define AUTO_UPDATE_MSW_CERTS 1`

**Alternate Designs**
PR #4545 partly solves this, but only for computers running currently supported versions of MS Windows. (Versions of MS Windows which are no longer supported by Microsoft do not get their certificate store updated automatically, though many can be updated manually by the user.)

Another approach would be to create mini-installers for each supported platform which update a new _ca-bundle.crt_ file from either BOINC, https://curl.se or Mozilla. But these require every BOINC user to be aware when a certificate is about to expire (or has expired) and to manually run the mini-installer.

**To Do:**
A chron job must be added to the BOINC server (currently on isaac) to periodically update the file 
`https://boinc.berkeley.edu/ca-bundle.crt` from either https://curl.se or Mozilla. I suggest doing this about every week or two, since https://curl.se updates it on their web site about every 6 weeks or so. This can be done with the following shell script:
`cd /home/boincadm/boinc-site/dl/`
`curl --remote-name --time-cond cacert.pem https://curl.se/ca/cacert.pem`
`if [  $? -ne 0 ]; then`
      `mv -f cacert.pem ca-bundle.crt`
`fi`

See https://curl.se/docs/caextract.html for more information.

title: Uploads Stopping for Projects with Large Files
body:
**The Problem** is that projects that upload large files tend to trigger errors such as "transient http error" that halts uploading. When this happens the only way to restart uploads for that computer is to reboot or restart the BOINC client. A consequence of this halt is that after a certain number of work units are in the upload queue it triggers "Not requesting tasks: too many uploads in progress" and downloads halt. After all work units complete the computer sits idle.
```
28618			10/29/2021 8:57:33 AM	Project communication failed: attempting access to reference site	
28619	World Community Grid	10/29/2021 8:57:33 AM	Temporarily failed upload of OPN1_0084321_00498_0_r1080501240_0: transient HTTP error	
28620	World Community Grid	10/29/2021 8:57:33 AM	Backing off 00:05:28 on upload of OPN1_0084321_00498_0_r1080501240_0
```
To reproduce use a 12c/24t or greater CPU to run 16 or more ARP1 work units to completion.
BOINC 7.6.16, Linux Mint 20.2, x86_64-pc-linux-gnu

**The Goal** is to allow any user with a bank of computers operating from a single IP address to run as many work units of any size for any BOINC project.
My goal is to turn in over 2,000 ARP work units per day which is 10% of that project's current daily progress. It doesn't seem in the spirit of BOINC to let a single simulation project run for over a year.

Anecdotal reports are that this does not happen when running a small number of large work units. My experience with ARP work units is that trying to run 16 ARP work units per 18c/36t computer is 100% guaranteed to fail and running 8 fails too often to endure. I'm currently trying 4 and 3 ARP work units but have already seen an upload seizure. Since ARP might not checkpoint for up to nine hours it wastes a lot of time either by dumping work or waiting for all work units to checkpoint. 

It's been suggested that it's caused by too many large files uploading at once. The use of <max_file_xfers_per_project> to restrict the number of concurrent uploads has offered no benefit in keeping uploads from seizing up.

It's been suggested that having too many computers running on the same IP address is part of the problem. I thought the objective of BOINC was to get as much work done as fast as possible.

It's been suggested that perhaps <max_nbytes> is being specified too low. The following is an example of a seized WU where ARP returns 7 files. Note that <max_nbytes> takes on 3 different values:

body: Signed-off-by: Vitalii Koshura <lestat.de.lionkur@gmail.com>

title: Upload File Control Needs To Be Segregated
body:
**The Problem** is insufficient file upload control. Currently there are two global commands available for use in the cc_config:
<max_file_xfers>64</max_file_xfers>, and
<max_file_xfers_per_project>4</max_file_xfers_per_project>.
They limit downloads the same as uploads when these need to be controlled separately. Those with slow internet may benefit from using <max_file_xfers>4</max_file_xfers> to maintain a reasonable file transfer rate without stalling transfers by attempting to transfer too many files at once.

Another issue is that World Community Grid (WCG) is considered a single project when it is really at present six projects: ARP, HST, MCM, OPN1/OPNG (uses a single server pipe), SCC and Beta. Several of these projects download large files but only ARP uploads large files at the completion of a work unit. I've had no problem downloading files and would like to allow the work server be in complete control with no governor to restrict download file flow.

A speed test of my ISP yields 38.1 Mbps download and 9.26 Mbps upload. Many ISPs throttle back the upload speed just so they can charge higher fees. Uploading large files like those produced by ARP need a governor. Attempting to upload too many large files increases the likelihood of stopping uploads altogether due to http transient errors. In the case of WCG only ARP needs to limit uploads. This issue could be mitigated by creating a project-specific command to use in our app_config project files. E.g.,
```
<app_config>
<!-- i9-9980XE   18c36t   32 GB   L3 Cache 24.75 MB  -->
    <app>
        <name>opng</name>
        <plan_class>opencl_nvidia_102</plan_class>
        <gpu_versions>
            <cpu_usage>1.0</cpu_usage>
            <gpu_usage>1.0</gpu_usage>
        </gpu_versions>
    </app>
    <app>
        <name>mcm1</name>
        <max_concurrent>15</max_concurrent>
    </app>
    <app>
        <name>opn1</name>
        <max_concurrent>15</max_concurrent>
    </app>
    <app>
        <name>arp1</name>
        <!-- needs 1 GB RAM per arp1 WU -->
        <max_concurrent>18</max_concurrent>

body: Re: https://github.com/BOINC/boinc/issues/2917 **Description of the Change** This branch replaces the menubar icons under macOS with new greyscale versions, to be consistent with design standards for macoS Mojave (10.14) and newer. The new menubar icons are higher-resolution and support light/dark mode. I've also increased the size of the `snooze`/`disconnect` indicators to make them more legible. ## Before ## After **Alternate Designs** I considered a few variations before coming up with these, and I've tried to make it relatively easy for others to modify them. Here are the steps (replace `boincdisconnect_macmenubar` with the name of the specific icon you want to replace in each step): 1. Open `boinc_macmenubar.psd` in any Photoshop-compatible image editor 2. Select the layers you want (e.g. "Boinc icon (light mode)" + "Disconnect" to generate the `boincdisconnect_macmenubar` icon) 3. Export as PNG to `clientugi/res/boincdisconnect_macmenubar.png` 4. In that dir, run `magick convert boincdisconnect_macmenubar.png -format xpm boincdisconnect_macmenubar.xpm` 5. Open that `.xpm` file in a text editor and change `static char *boincdisconnect_macmenubar[]` to `static const char *boincdisconnect_macmenubar_xpm[]` --- **This is WIP because the [`wxSystemAppearance::IsDark()`](https://docs.wxwidgets.org/trunk/classwx_system_appearance.html) call doesn't appear to be returning the correct result. In my tests (under macOS Monterey), it consistently returned `false`. Further, just getting the correct value at initialization time isn't sufficient, because we need to be able to change the icon as the system switches between light/dark modes. wxWidgets has that capability (via the [`wxSysColourChangedEvent`](https://docs.wxwidgets.org/3.0/classwx_sys_colour_changed_event.html) class), but wiring it up is a bit of a challenge. I'd appreciate some assistance with that. It's possible that binding the color change event will address the issue I'm seeing with `IsDark()`. My guess is that `wxWidgets` initially assumes that `IsDark()` is `false`, then updates that internal value later.

title: client: fix work-fetch logic when max concurrent limits are used
body:
The round-robin simulation would stop simulating jobs for a project
once a max concurrent limit (app or project) was reached.
As a result it would decide there was a shortfall,
and keep requesting work up to the limit of 1000 jobs.

To fix this:
1) keep simulating a project after an MCL is reached
2) for each (project, resource) pair, keep track of the latest
    simulation time T when an MCL was reached.
3) for such a project, don't request work for a resource if
    T > now + work buf size

This allows us, e.g., to request GPU jobs from a project
even if its CPU jobs (taking MCL into account) fill the buffer.

This works in the simulation case that showed the problem (#192).

Also: add a bit more logging, and improve names

title: [Feature Request][vboxwrapper]Enable vboxwrapper to use VirtualBox differencing images
body:
**Describe the problem**

Some BOINC projects using VirtualBox/vboxwrapper deal with large vdi image files.

Typical examples 
LHC@home: 700 MB - 2.9 GB
Rosetta@home: > 7 GB


The traditional method to handle those files is:
1. Download a compressed image to the projects folder and expand it there
2. When a task starts, copy the expanded image file to slots/n/vm_image.vdi
3. vboxwrapper attaches that vm_image.vdi as hdd for r/w operations while the task executes


**Describe the solution you'd like**

Use multiattach mode images together with differencing images.

Both are VirtualBox features for many years.
See:
[https://www.virtualbox.org/manual/ch05.html#hdimagewrites](https://www.virtualbox.org/manual/ch05.html#hdimagewrites)
[https://www.virtualbox.org/manual/ch05.html#diffimages](https://www.virtualbox.org/manual/ch05.html#diffimages)

This would allow to change the method above as follows:
1. Don't copy the image file from the projects folder to the slots/n folder.
Instead, use the image file in the projects folder as (readonly) parent for all tasks.
2. Vboxwrapper configures the VM to automatically create a corresponding differencing image for each task in the task's snapshot folder.
All data a VM writes to disk will go to that differencing image.


**Additional context**


_Benefits_

The new method avoids lots of data being copied while a tasks starts which makes this phase faster.
It also saves lots of disk space on computers running many affected tasks concurrently.
Example from LHC@home (CMS subproject):

traditional method
initial vdi size: 2.9 GB (CMS_2021_07_07.vdi -> vm_image.vdi)
end of task size: 3.9 GB (vm_image.vdi) after 12 h

new method
differencing image size: growing from 2 MB to 1.0 GB within 12 h


_Other Requirements_

- a modified vboxwrapper has to be used.
- project admins can switch between the old/new method using <multiattach_vdi_file>filename.vdi</multiattach_vdi_file> in vbox_job.xml.
- project admins need to remove the <copy_file/> tag from the task template.


_Additional Comment_

I'm currently testing the new method on a couple of Linux computers with CMS tasks from LHC@home.
Can't test it on Windows since I don't have a development environment to compile the vboxwrapper there.
I also don't run Rosetta's vbox app but I'm sure they would also benefit a lot.

title: [WIP] Check for idle time settings that preventing computing
body:
**Description of the Change**
As I worked on #4600 I found it was possible for a user to set their computing preferences in a way that does not allow any computing.  If "suspend when not idle" is enabled, and "suspend if idle for" is set to >0, it is possible for the computer to not process any tasks if the first setting is greater than the second.  This commit checks for this condition, and if true, will generate an error message.  The user will have to modify one of the values in order to save their preferences.

![Suspend min-max error message](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/58096400/153793499-7c07c14e-cb4d-4739-bb26-d47ad2f3ab13.PNG)

This PR is a work in progress.  The commit only checks for local preferences in BOINC Manger.  There are a few things I am not familiar with and could use some assistance:

- [ ] This does not fix web preferences.  I feel the bug is a bigger concern with web settings since someone can make an accidental change and affect multiple computers.  I see there is code in the html directory, but I don't know if revising the code here will make the correction for all projects to follow.  I can make an attempt to fix this on the web side, I just don't know the relation of this code to the separate projects.
- [ ] I am not familiar with localization.  I'm not sure if anything needs to be done to get the new error message translated.  I'd be happy to help if someone could point me in the right direction.
- [ ] This doesn't check existing settings in global_prefs(_override).xml when loading BOINC.  Someone could manually set this, or could have had this setting accidentally and not know it.  I don't know how critical it is to check for this.

Also, there are a few small items I would like a second opinion on:

1. The warning I generated is called a validation error.  I think technically this is incorrect, it should be an error.  Both numbers are validated prior to the comparison.  I can make a different dialogue box, but I was trying to keep the code simple.
2. I am open to suggestions to changes to the warning message I created.  I'm not sure I am happy with how it reads.  I'm trying to keep the message short and simple, not long and complicated.

title: BOINC switching GPUs between tasks on multi-GPU systems
body:
**Describe the bug**
When you are using more than one GPU for BOINC on a single system, the client tends to pointlessly switch cards between tasks after restarting (or perhaps it's random and there is a 50/50 etc. chance of the "wrong" card being used, I haven't looked into that exactly). This cannot be prevented in any way that I was able to figure out (you could run a client for each card or do it manually by suspending tasks and resuming them in such an order that it forces the tasks onto the GPUs of your choosing, but that level of micromanagement is obviously not a desirable solution). The "Switch between tasks every X minutes" option has no effect on this, by the way. I have it set to the maximum of 9999 minutes (why is there no option to never switch anyway?), and while I guess it prevents switching during sessions for that theoretical amount of time, if you restart the client all bets are off again.

For some projects this isn't a problem, but GPUGrid for instance is very sensitive to switching GPUs. You cannot continue tasks on a different card. It will yield an immediate computation error in that case, often resulting in quite a lot of lost work (tasks can take up to a day or more, depending on the card).

**Steps To Reproduce**
1.  Attach to GPUGrid on a system with more than one GPU, crunch GPU tasks. Any GPU project will do, really, but you'll notice it right away with that one.
2.  Restart the client.
3. If the tasks error out you'll know that there's been a switch. (stderr output: `ERROR: /home/user/conda/conda-bld/acemd3_1632842613607/work/src/mdsim/context.cpp line 318: Cannot use a restart file on a different device!`)

EDIT: Actually it looks like there's switching even during the same uninterrupted session if computation is automatically suspended (ex. because of an exclusive app running)...

**Expected behavior**
Keep the same card on the same task from start to finish. There should be no need to switch in 99% of cases.

title: Limit number of VirtualBox tasks
body: On AMD processors where the user's trying to interact with the machine, lots of VB tasks can make the interface very sluggish.  There's currently no way to limit this, apart from at project level.  But if I limit LHC to do only x VB tasks, and also Rosetta, if both happen to be running, I get double the VBs I want.  A global limit would be more useful, preferably with an option for number of tasks and number of cores to give more flexibility.

title: Task action: "Suspend after next checkpoint"
body:
**Describe the problem**
On client shutdown or task suspend, non-checkpointed work is lost. So far, I've found uncheckpointed work for 1h or even 2h worth, which is quite a waste, if stopped and lost.
When an orderly shutdown is possible (eg. reviewing tasks before shutdown/restart), you can wait tasks to checkpoint before suspending/quitting, but it's tedious and inconvenient.
It can be helpful when shutting down, but also for switching tasks/projects.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I would like to have a 'Suspend after next checkpoint' task action. Thus, I could send it to all running tasks to guarantee that no work is lost.

**Additional context**
Assumptions:
* Tasks notify client on checkpoint, which can react accordingly.
* Some tasks do not checkpoint, which is fine. It's up to you to know it if you intend to do "whatever at checkpoint".

This feature would later enable also a 'checkpointed shutdown' for the whole client. You can manually trigger it as a command when winding down before shutdown, set it as an opt-in behaviour on `SIGTERM` or do it on another signal. Lots of people might find it helpful to avoid wasted work (time and electricity).

title: [WEB] Deprecated: Passing null parameter to function trim()
body:
**Describe the bug**
`Deprecated: trim(): Passing null to parameter #1 ($string) of type string is deprecated in /html/inc/boinc_db.inc on line 147`
According to [PHP Deprecated Features manual](https://www.php.net/manual/en/migration81.deprecated.php#migration81.deprecated.core.null-not-nullable-internal), it is no longer possible to pass null to the trim function in PHP 8.1. 


**Recommendation**
As discussed on [Laravel](https://github.com/laravel/framework/issues/41643) and  [Symfony](https://github.com/symfony/symfony/issues/45179) replacing  `null` with the empty string `''` when setting a default 'empty' value that will be passed on to trim() will resolve the error.
On [boinc_db.inc line 147](https://github.com/BOINC/boinc/edit/master/html/inc/boinc_db.inc#L147) we can : 
> ```diff
> -return $db->base_escape_string(trim($string));
> +return $db->base_escape_string(trim((string) $string));
> ```
according to [php.net/manual](https://www.php.net/manual/en/language.types.string.php#language.types.string.casting) `null` is always converted to an empty string when casting to string. 

**System Information**
 - OS: UBUNTU 22.04
- PHP Version: 8.1

title: Deadlines missed if running multi-thread and single thread projects
body:
**Describe the bug**
If running multi-thread and single thread projects, the scheduler often leaves the single thread ones too late.

**Steps To Reproduce**
1. Run only a single-thread project.
2. Set no new tasks for that project and allow new tasks for a multi-thread project, such that the multi-thread project will fill all threads with 1 task.
3. Wait until the number of single thread tasks becomes less than the number of threads you have available.
4. The scheduler will run multi-thread tasks only, until the last minute, then run single threads in panic mode at the same time (therefore more slowly) and miss the deadline.

**Expected behaviour**
The single thread tasks need to be started earlier, or the multi-thread tasks need to be suspended.

**System Information**
 - OS: Windows 11
 - BOINC Version: 7.20

title: BOINC does not gracefully handle capitalization discrepancies
body:
**Describe the bug**
When using boinccmd (and I believe the underlying GUI-RPC as well), inputting a project url with a capitalization different than BOINC's internal list of project URLs results in a "no such project" response.

**Steps To Reproduce**
1. Find a project url attached to your BOINC client such as https://sech.me/boinc/Amicable/
2. Run the command `boinccmd --project https://sech.me/boinc/amicable/ nomorework`
3. BOINC will respond with `GUI RPC error: No such project
Operation failed: Error -1`
4. Re-run the command with the correct capitalization: `boinccmd --project https://sech.me/boinc/Amicable/ nomorework`
5. Command completed successfully

**Expected behavior**
While URLs may indeed be case-sensitive, this error message does not clearly indicate to the user what they are doing wrong. I would prefer that BOINC notice the difference in capitalization and resolve this internally, there is no reason to expect two separate boinc projects would exist at the same URL and be separated only by a difference in capitalization. 

**System Information**
 - OS:  Ubuntu 20.04 LTS
 - BOINC Version: 7.16.6 x86_64-pc-linux-gnu

title: build fcgi_file_upload_handler w/o mysql libs
body:
The file_upload_handlers don't access the DB. Consequently, and correctly, the "file_upload_handler" doesn't link the MYSQLLIBS. However, the fcgi version still does. This patch fixes this, i.e. it builds the "fcgi_file_upload_handler" without linking the MYSQLLIBS (which are contained in the SERVERLIBS_FCGI).

(FWIW the use case here is that we are running the same fcgi_file_upload_handler binary on multiple servers, which we are upgrading to a new OS version one by one. So the same binary has to run on servers with different library versions. The only library that we don't have a backport for in the upgraded version is the libmysqlclient. So we like to get this out of the way since it's not used by the file_upload_handler anyway)

title: [CI] Single job on PRs only
body:
Single job on PRs only.

From here:
https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-workflows/workflow-syntax-for-github-actions#example-using-a-fallback-value

> If you build the group name with a property that is only defined for specific events, you can use a fallback value. For example, github.head_ref is only defined on pull_request events. If your workflow responds to other events in addition to pull_request events, you will need to provide a fallback to avoid a syntax error. The following concurrency group cancels in-progress jobs or runs on pull_request events only; if github.head_ref is undefined, the concurrency group will fallback to the run ID, which is guaranteed to be both unique and defined for the run.
> ```yaml
> concurrency: 
>   group: ${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}
>   cancel-in-progress: true
> ```

**Describe the bug**
In advanced view of BOINC Manager, the user has the ability to hide columns.  If a column is hidden, changes are accepted, then made visible again, that column is moved to be the last column, regardless of where it was prior to hiding it.

**Steps To Reproduce**
1. Open BOINC Manager, Advanced View.
2. "Options"->"Select Columns..."
3. Unselect any column that is not the last for its tab (Project is a great example), click Save.
4. Open "Select Columns..." again.  The column that is hidden has now moved in this window to the last location.
5. Selecting this column, then clicking Save will bring the column back, but now it is the last column.

**Expected behavior**
It would be ideal if the column would be restored to its original place.

**Screenshots**
Item 3 above, before hitting Save:

title: Avoid gcc warnings
body:
If '-Wunused-result' is set compilers usually print a warning when they expect a function to return 'something' but that 'something' is not used in the subsequent code.
The usual method to omit the warning is to precede the function call with '(void)'.

In case of gcc this doesn't work for years:
```
switcher.cpp: In function ‘int main(int, char**)’:
switcher.cpp:118:26: warning: ignoring return value of ‘int setgid(__gid_t)’ declared with attribute ‘warn_unused_result’ [-Wunused-result]
  118 |             (void) setgid(grp->gr_gid);
      |                    ~~~~~~^~~~~~~~~~~~~
switcher.cpp:125:26: warning: ignoring return value of ‘int setuid(__uid_t)’ declared with attribute ‘warn_unused_result’ [-Wunused-result]
  125 |             (void) setuid(pw->pw_uid);
      |                    ~~~~~~^~~~~~~~~~~~

```

title: fix non-BOINC CPU usage limit on Win and Linux
body:
Fixes #4327, #4328

The pref "suspend_cpu_usage" lets you suspend BOINC computing
when the non-BOINC CPU usage (NBCU) exceeds a threshold T.

NBCU excludes BOINC-related processes
- the BOINC client
- the BOINC Manager
- BOINC apps and their process trees
- graphics apps
- VBox daemon
    This can use significant time.
    We count it as BOINC-related only if BOINC is running a Vbox app

NBCU also excludes low-priority processors:
"niced" on Linux, idle class on Win.
We don't want such processes to keep BOINC from computing.

This preference is enforced every 10 seconds.
The client estimates the NBCU over the last 10 sec,
and suspends BOINC processing if the load exceeds T

Currently, NBCU is estimated by scanning the list of all processes,
skipping the types of processes listed above,
and adding up the user and kernel time of others.
This gives a value Tcur.
Let Tprev be the previous value (from 10 seconds ago).
Let X = (Tcur - Tprev)/(ncpus*10).
We suspend processing if X/(ncpus*10) > T

This approach is fundamentally flawed.
It would be fine if processes never exited.
But if a process exits during a given 10-sec period,
its time is included in Tprev but not Tcur,
in which case X is wrong; it may be negative.
This can cause false negatives (not suspending when we should have suspended).

To fix this, we need a different approach.
We shouldn't estimate total CPU by adding up current processes.
Fortunately, most OS's have an API for getting total CPU time.
On Linux this is broken down into a lot of categories,
including "niced" processes.
On Win it's only broken down by user/kernel.

The new approach is basically:
every 10 sec, get the increase Y in total CPU (as reported by the OS).
Then estimate the total CPU time B
used by BOINC-related and low-priority processes in the last 10 sec,
and let X = Y - B.
Suspend processing if X/(ncpus*10) > T

We'll estimate B by scanning the process list and adding up
the totals for BOINC-related processes,
and computing the delta since 10 sec ago.
This is subject to the same error as above:
when these processes exit, B will be underestimated (typically negative),
so X will be overestimated, causing a false positive.
However, this happens infrequently;
BOINC jobs low-priority processes are generally long-running.
And we can avoid false positives by setting X to zero if B is negative.

Because of the possible error in X,
we'll use a conservative approach to resuming from a suspension:
if we're currently suspended because of CPU usage,
unsuspend only if X < T for two consecutive 10-sec periods

title: [CI][OSX] Verify build for universal libraries
body:
In #4849 universal lib verification was added to cmake build.

The next code need to be adapted to verify in general CI flow ( https://github.com/BOINC/boinc/blob/master/mac_build/buildMacBOINC-CI.sh ) after **every** target the files that were built during each particular target.

```
echo "Testing libs and binaries for univaral build."
echo ""

binaries_libs_list="*.a boinc switcher gfx_switcher boincscr setprojectgrp boinccmd SetUpSecurity AddRemoveUser BOINCManager PostInstall BOINCSaver *Installer Uninstall*"
folders_list="3rdParty/buildCache/mac/lib mac_build/build/Deployment"

for object in $binaries_libs_list; do
    echo "Search for: $object"
    found_list=$(find $folders_list -type f -name "$object")
    if [ -z "$found_list" ]; then
        echo "ERROR: $object not found"
        exit 1
    fi
    find $folders_list -type f -name "$object" -exec sh -c '
    for f do
        echo "Test : $f"
        if ! lipo "$f" -verify_arch x86_64 arm64; then
            echo "Fail: $(basename $f) is not universal"
            lipo -info "$f"
            exit 1
        fi         
    done
    ' sh {} +; 
done
```

This will help to see where the issue happens (if any) and have a list of affected binaries and the targets they were built in.

title: client: close file descriptors if Curl initialization fails.
body:
HTTP_OP::libcurl_exec() opens input and/or output files.
    In the normal case these eventually are closed in handle_messages()
    when the HTTP op finishes.
    But if the call to curl_multi_add_handle() returns an error
    (which I believe happens on a connect failure, e.g. if the project is down)
    then we need to close the files.
    We weren't doing this, possibly leading to running out of file descriptors.

Fixes #4914 (possibly)

title: [Feature] Provide limit checks when reading global_prefs_override
body:
**Describe the problem**
Preferences can be modified in three ways:

1. Web preferences
2. Locally, via the Manger
3. Locally, by editing the global_prefs_override.xml file directly

When changing preferences via the project website or the Manager, those values are validated to be in the correct range.  However, when BOINC is started, it will read the global_prefs_override file (if it exists), and store those values.  Some of those preferences are currently validated, but not all.  The example below shows the percentage of CPUs being changed to a range between 0 and 100:
https://github.com/BOINC/boinc/blob/3fc6c024711175413eb9e57c53fad1a78267274e/lib/prefs.cpp#L509-L513

However, if suspend_cpu_usage were accidentally edited as a negative number, that negative number would be stored, and BOINC would never crunch any tasks.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I feel this can be resolved with two steps:
1. For any double variables that don't have limits set already, add them.  These limits are likely to be simple, such as setting a negative number to 0.  This will have to be evaluated on a case-by-case basis.
2. The user should be aware that BOINC had to modify one of their values.  I think the best thing would be to create a message in the notices tab.  I would think this would be similar to how a message appears when there is incorrect data in an app_config file.  The message doesn't have to be too specific, perhaps which preference was changed.  I would assume if the user is editing their global_prefs_override file, they will know how to read through it and find the error.

**Additional context**
I have started to work on this solution, but with #4871 being in development, I stopped so I didn't have to redo large sections of code.  I would be happy to continue developing it after that PR is merged.  In the meantime, I'm looking for any feedback.

title: Linux: downstream releases broken in specific repositories
body:
Mainstream Linux releases of the BOINC client / manager packages are handled by repo teams. But problems rebound by causing reputational damage to BOINC and, ultimately, UCB.

There have been sporadic grumblings for some time about an inability to run repository installations of BOINC for versions of Linux such as Ubuntu 22.04 LTS and Mint 21. None of them were specific enough for us to be able to pinpoint the source of the problem.

A conversation I had yesterday on the BOINC message board finally seems to identify the answer. We went from

> I upgraded linux mint to v21 about a month ago. I've been T/S off and on since but have reached a point of giving up.

via a single piece of advice to

> Hot damn! That did it...I'm back in business.
> Thank you!

(source: https://boinc.berkeley.edu/forum_thread.php?id=14792)

The advice was to **discard** the version 18.1 of BOINC supplied by the repositories, and replace it with version 20.2: I suggested @LocutusOfBorg's PPA as the source.

Version 18.1 was **never released** by BOINC for any desktop OS (Apple, Linux, or Windows). It was exclusively an Android release. It now appears likely that the desktop source code included in https://github.com/BOINC/boinc/tree/client_release/7/7.18 is seriously broken.

Now that we have had a reliable, recommended, release version 7.20.2 for over 2 months, working on all three platforms (although the platforms supported are not made clear in https://github.com/BOINC/boinc/releases), I suggest that we take urgent, proactive, action to get v7.18.1 **removed** from any Linux package that may have been inadvertently published, and get it replaced by v7.20.2

As an unknown, independent, volunteer, my voice won't carry enough weight to achieve that by itself. It needs to be an authoritative, clear, release instruction from a known BOINC source in the Linux arena - @davidpanderson, @lfield, or @AenBleidd come to mind.

It would also be helpful if Linux users with package maintenance connections (@Germano0, @LocutusOfBorg) could help to reinforce the message.

title: Make BOINC urls case-insensitive
body:
**Describe the problem**
When a user is given a URL to attach to a BOINC project, it will not work if the case is not correct. For example: boincproject.com/boinc would work but boincproject.com/BOINC would not. Domain names are case-insensitive, and I see no reason for case-sensitive URL handling. There is a chance that a user without the correct case-sensitive URL may try to attach to a project and therefore have issues doing so. Making URL handling case-insensitive would eliminate this source of error and confusion.

This is a further extension of https://github.com/BOINC/boinc/issues/4801

I realize this is a small issue and there are more important ones, just wanted to raise it as an idea.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Make BOINC server URL handling case-insensitive

title: Client: are we using curl efficiently?
body:
The new managers of World Community Grid are struggling to optimize their network connectivity. For me, the major problems are with downloading task datafiles following a successful scheduler contact. The logs sometimes throw up questions worth discussing. Here's the full log of one such download connection. [WCG_download_failure.log](https://github.com/BOINC/boinc/files/9715387/WCG_download_failure.log) This particular log was captured from BOINC v7.20.2, running under Linux Mint 20.3 Some extracts of interest: ``` Oct 05 08:53:34 Michelle boinc[1678]: 05-Oct-2022 08:53:34 [World Community Grid] [http] [ID#45505] Received header from server: HTTP/2 503 Oct 05 08:53:34 Michelle boinc[1678]: 05-Oct-2022 08:53:34 [World Community Grid] [http] [ID#45505] Received header from server: cache-control: no-cache Oct 05 08:53:34 Michelle boinc[1678]: 05-Oct-2022 08:53:34 [World Community Grid] [http] [ID#45505] Received header from server: content-type: text/html Oct 05 08:53:34 Michelle boinc[1678]: 05-Oct-2022 08:53:34 [World Community Grid] [http] [ID#45505] Received header from server: Oct 05 08:53:34 Michelle boinc[1678]: 05-Oct-2022 08:53:34 [World Community Grid] [http] [ID#45505] Received header from server:

503 Service Unavailable

Oct 05 08:53:34 Michelle boinc[1678]: 05-Oct-2022 08:53:34 [World Community Grid] [http] [ID#45505] Received header from server: No server is available to handle this request. Oct 05 08:53:34 Michelle boinc[1678]: 05-Oct-2022 08:53:34 [World Community Grid] [http] [ID#45505] Received header from server: ``` I don't think we make any attempt to capture, interpret and report these useful messages. Should we? ``` Oct 05 08:53:34 Michelle boinc[1678]: 05-Oct-2022 08:53:34 [World Community Grid] [http] [ID#45505] Info: Connection cache is full, closing the oldest one. Oct 05 08:53:34 Michelle boinc[1678]: 05-Oct-2022 08:53:34 [World Community Grid] [http] [ID#45505] Info: Closing connection 22618 ``` This information message can't be found in client source code - we're assuming it's generated by curl. The difference between oldest and newest connection IDs is some 20k - does our cache really get that big? Should it? My attention has been drawn to https://curl.se/libcurl/c/CURLMOPT_MAXCONNECTS.html - which suggests that the maximum number of multi-use connections can be limited. Should we use that facility?

title: BOINC 7.18.1 client refuse to start with specific CPU.
body:
**Describe the bug**
The BOINC client refuse to run/load [as a service] with a Pentium G3240T present (_probably the same with a number of other Pentium G family CPUs too_)

**Steps To Reproduce**
1. Normal install procedure, including OpenCL.
2. A error message is generated when trying to start the client - STATUS=4/ILL.

**System Information**
 - OS: Lubuntu 22.04.1 LTS
 - BOINC Version: 7.18.1

**Additional context**
Less than two weeks ago, I got my hands on six refurbished _Dell OptiPlex 3020 Micro_ and started to prepare them last weekend. Tried to run the client on the first and it failed. Tried the remaining five and those failed the very same way (_which rules out any faulty CPU_). I suspected that the issue is CPU related anyway. Didn't bother much at the time, as I already had ordered a better CPU, an i7-4785T, to test if it was possible to upgrade beyond Dell's official specifications (_4th gen. i5/35W. It's not unusual that the hw manufacturers don't update their manuals._) The BOINC system requirements [Linux] specify Pentium 500 MHz or greater (_ie. Pentium III [or a Mendocino family/2nd gen. Celeron]_). The OptiFlex 3020M originally fit Pentium G3240T is a Haswell CPU @2.70 GHz, so it should have been working.

I got the i7-4785T earlier this week and tested it immediately without any issues - the BOINC client is running fine. The main feature differences between the CPUs are that the G3240T lack support for Hyper-Threading, vPro and some extra AES instructions (_other than having no Turbo Boost, less cores/threads and cache than the 4785T_) If any of these three are required, it should be included in the system requirements.

Related to BOINC, I have so far come across different [Debian/Ubuntu] error messages (_STATUS=..._), which I have searched on the Internet and have not found any relevant/useful explanations. One of them is earlier reported here.

title: GPU time left is wildly inaccurate for projects with more than one GPU app
body:
**Describe the bug**
For projects such as Primegrid with many GPU apps, if Boinc is used to seeing one of them, then gets a different one, the "time left" estimate is wildly inaccurate.

For example, I currently have a genefer_extreme task which has reached about halfway in 2 days.  So sensibly, we'd say the other half would take two days aswell.  But it has an estimate of 36 days.  This completely screws up scheduling for other projects on that GPU, as it believes the Primegrid task will not reach the deadline, and enters panic mode.

**Steps To Reproduce**
1. Run Primegrid on small tasks on GPU, such as genefer 15 (the smallest GPU task).
2. Switch Primegrid to do genefer_extreme (the largest GPU task).
3. Let it run for a bit and observe the crazy estimate of remaining time.

**System Information**
 - OS: Windows 11
 - BOINC Version: 7.20.2

**Additional context**
Perhaps Boinc could concentrate less on assuming the task could be non-linear in progress, and concentrate more on how long this one has taken so far?  Or perhaps record how long each app takes?  It would appear currently Boinc is not allowing for multiple GPU apps from one project.

title: Create "Apple" GPU scheduling group
body:
Currently there are three hardcoded scheduling groups for GPUs, Nvidia, AMD, and Intel.

When a Mac requests a task for GPU, it does so as an unknown vendor and includes the full description; ie "Apple M1"

The server must know "Apple M1" as a coprocessor in order to send tasks. However, there's now an Apple M1 Max, M1 Pro, M1 Ultra, M2... with more to come. On the server side, each of these must be individually hard coded; currently 8(?) with the probability of continuous changes in the future.

If "Apple" was also a scheduling group, all Mxxxxx GPUs would be lumped together by the client as "Apple GPU" and the server would only have one "thing" to deal with. I realize this requires a change to both client and server, and would only work with those running up-to-date code on both sides, but it would be an improvement. At the least, a project could say "if you're running a Mac M3 ProUltraMaxExtreme or newer, you must use BOINC 7.22.7 or later" instead of having a list a mile long.

body:
With GCC 12, this header file cannot be included on its own. Doing so fails with #error, but also produces many warnings related to implicit ints and implicit function declarations. This is inconvenient for distributions who are trying to switch to newer C versions (without implicit ints/function declarations), and monitor builds for suspicious warnings related to obsolete C features.

Related to:

title: Potential SQL Injection Vulnerability in Default BOINC Website
body:
I'm a developer for MilkyWay@home, and our project recently failed a routine vulnerability scan from our host institution. The potential vulnerability comes from the "next_url" parameter in the BOINC website file "create_account_form.php" (link to the relevant code on github here https://github.com/BOINC/boinc/blob/master/html/user/create_account_form.php). From what I understand, the vulnerability is this: if you put something in the website url after "create_account_form.php", like "create_account_form.php?next_url=1", then the page reloads but everything after the ? persists in the url. I'm told that this is difficult but not impossible to utilize for a SQL injection attack. Here's the full report that we got from our routine vulnerability scan: ``` Using the GET HTTP method, Nessus found that : + The following resources may be vulnerable to blind SQL injection : + The 'next_url' parameter of the /milkyway/create_account_form.php CGI : /milkyway/create_account_form.php?next_url='+and+'b'>'a -------- output --------

If you already have an account and want to run Mil [...]

-------- vs --------

If you already have an account and want to run Mil [...]

------------------------ ``` This looks like the scan was able to access unintended php source code for this webpage via the url line. We would like to fix this issue so that it isn't a problem in the future. However, I don't have any experience with this sort of thing, and I was wondering if any of you who knew more could help us out. Additionally, we wanted to bring it to your attention so that the BOINC website code could get fixed, so that other people don't experience any issues from this in the future. It looks like the BOINC code tries to sanitize the "next_url" parameter with the function "sanitize_local_url" in https://github.com/BOINC/boinc/blob/master/html/inc/util.inc. Maybe this sanitize function can be changed in some way to prevent this problem? Or maybe there's a better fix. I also posted about this on the boinc forums [here](https://boinc.berkeley.edu/forum_thread.php?id=14904&postid=110987#110987) but they recommended that I post the issue here instead. Let me know if you'd like any more information about the issue and I'm happy to share.

title: client: don't send "web prefs" in scheduler requests.
body:
This was originally done to propagate prefs between projects.
When you edit prefs on project A, they propagate to project B and you can edit them there too.
But this doesn't make sense - and can lead to undesirable behavior - when projects
have different prefs-editing web code.
And it's not a particularly useful feature.
If you're using web prefs, the Manager tells you what project they came from.
You can go there to edit them.

Note: we still send working prefs,, which are used for scheduler decisions.
