title: Notices and warnings on docker installation are confusing and putting off volunteers
body:
### Describe the bug

Abstract

From volunteer feedback we see that unspecific and persistent recommendations about installing Docker in recent BOINC installer/client/manager put off volunteers of projects that don't use that. We therefore ask to remove these messages from general BOINC and let the respective projects inform volunteers what for and how to install Docker.

Details

On a recent public event, presenting Einstein@Home (E@H), we were approached by quite a few people who, for one reason or another, had to (re-)install BOINC. When they were recommended to install Docker, they got quite confused e.g. for not knowing Docker. Some of them even stopped installing BOINC and thus supporting E@H because of either their confusion - or they just plain didn't want to install Docker and didn't know whether E@H would work without it.

Installing Docker on Windows is not trivial. It's not a simple additional software: you have to enable WSL, which requires at least one reboot, and, depending on your system, even modifying BIOS settings. Then you need to install the BOINC WSL image. Generally, having to read, understand and follow hard to find, English-only instructions [1] can easily discourage any casual volunteer. We also don't think that [2] is a viable solution for these volunteers because, again, every additional click, page to read and prerequisite to fulfill is an additional chance of losing prospective users.

Thus issuing a general recommendation in the manager's notifications, and, even worse, a repeating warning (in red, without further details) in the log is the wrong approach in our opinion. Let the projects decide to issue such notifications and how. They can provide tailored information about why and how they use Docker such that volunteers can make an informed decision about installing it. Speaking of projects: how many active projects do actually require Docker as the message suggests?

Docker might be useful for some projects but, in all honesty, it can arguably only be set up by a minority of skilled users. Based on the numerous feedback we got, the average casual user that just wants to support a standard BOINC project should not be bothered with it. They even entirely stop short of using BOINC. That hurts not only single projects, but the BOINC ecosystem as a whole.

Summarizing, in our opinion BOINC:

- should remove the general recommendation to install Docker from the installer, notices and client messages and instead let projects that do need it take care of informing voulunteers about what Docker is needed for and how to install it (e.g. via news and join instructions)

- could add the Docker icon to the list of "Supported systems" shown in the project details area (when adding a project in the Manager). Note, this list doesn't seem to fully match [3] where Docker support is already listed (and might probably even be wrong for LHC@Home: i.e. VirtualBox vs. Docker). While at it, please refresh the icons used in the manager to match those of [3].

- could offer to install Docker when adding projects **and** a selected project does support docker, according to the "Supported systems" spec. If so, offer it in a very optional and fully automated way (along the lines of [2]?).

Thanks,
Einstein@Home
(Bernd Machenschalk, Heinz-Bernd Eggenstein, Oliver Behnke, Alexander Post)

[1] https://github.com/BOINC/boinc/wiki/Installing-Docker-on-Windows
[2] https://github.com/BOINC/boinc-buda-runner-wsl-installer
[3] https://boinc.berkeley.edu/projects.php

title: Android: update build toolchain to Gradle 9.5.1 / AGP 9.3.1
body:
Fixes #6926

**Description of the Change**

Updates the Android build toolchain from Gradle 8.12 / AGP 8.0.1 to Gradle 9.5.1 / AGP 9.3.1. This snowballed a bit because AGP 9 removes a few things the old build relied on. Here's what changed and why:

- Release builds now run R8 with optimizations. AGP 9 dropped support for `proguard-android.txt`, so the optimize profile is the only option now. I smoke-tested a release build on an Android 14 emulator with real client binaries from CI: the app launches, the native client starts and runs, and attaching to a project works. More eyes on real devices before a release wouldn't hurt.
- I rewrote the armv6 asset stripping because AGP 9 removed the legacy `applicationVariants` API. New `verifyArmv6_*AssetsStripped` tasks fail the armv6 builds if binaries for other ABIs ever end up in the merged assets. I checked the guards actually fire by breaking the stripping on purpose.
- One source change: `SettingsFragment.onSharedPreferenceChanged` takes a nullable key as of SDK 34 (null shows up when preferences are cleared). There's a new test covering it.
- `MonitorTest`'s platform detection tests depended on the machine running them (they passed on Linux CI but failed on my Mac). They now pin `os.arch` and cover the whole architecture mapping table.
- Added `org.junit.platform:junit-platform-launcher` since Gradle 9 no longer ships it, removed the Jetifier flag (nothing needs it anymore), and fixed all the deprecation warnings. The build is clean under `--warning-mode all`, so the eventual Gradle 10 jump should be less painful.

**Alternate Designs**

I considered a smaller bump to the latest Gradle 8.x (keeping AGP 8.x) to keep the change contained, but in #6926 AenBleidd asked for the latest stable version, so I did the full jump. For R8 I also considered keeping optimizations off with `-dontoptimize` keep rules, but went with the profile AGP 9 expects plus the emulator smoke test instead.

**Release Notes**

Android: updated the build toolchain to Gradle 9.5.1 and Android Gradle Plugin 9.3.1. Release builds are now R8-optimized.

title: client: fix swap limit stopping jobs from running
body: Fixes #7132 and #7146. In both cases the swap limit stops jobs from running even though nothing is swapping. On Linux the client estimates an unstarted job's swap usage from the app version's max RSS, which is the wrong quantity. It charges a job for memory it may never swap out, so with 8 GB of swap and a 4 GB app you get two jobs no matter what. I now track max swap usage separately. When nothing is swapping that's zero, so it imposes no limit. On Android swap is zram, which the RAM limit already covers and which you can't resize without root. I excluded it there, the same way it already is on macOS. Three other things turned up while I was in there. `procinfo_app()` counts a process twice when an app reports a helper PID that is also a descendant of its main process, the swap-kill scheduler can stall the client permanently, and `defaults()` sets `vm_max_used_frac` twice. Details are in the commit messages. Each commit stands alone and builds. I tested the Android and desktop clients. I couldn't exercise the swap-kill and revive paths, since they need real swap pressure with `vm_max_used_frac` below 100%. I think this is worth releasing sooner than usual. The client simply runs fewer tasks than it should. Happy to change anything or drop parts of it. I'd rather see the problem fixed than these particular patches merged, and if the approach is wrong, I hope it is still useful. title: Android: client binaries are 4 KB aligned and fail to load on 16 KB page-size devices
body:
### Describe the bug

While emulator-testing #7193 I hit this: on Android system images with a 16 KB page size (the google_apis_ps16k images), the BOINC app UI runs but the native client never starts. The Monitor logs `getPidForProcessName(): /data/user/0/edu.berkeley.boinc/client/boinc not found in ps output!` and retries `connect failure: IO` forever, and the app sits on the splash screen. The same APK works fine on a standard 4 KB image (Android 14, API 34).

The cause is ELF alignment. The client binaries shipped in the app assets are linked with 4 KB load segment alignment: I checked the program headers of the current CI-built binaries and both x86_64 and arm64-v8a have PT_LOAD alignment 0x1000. A 16 KB kernel refuses to load such executables, which from the app's side looks like the client silently never starting.

This matters beyond emulators. Google requires 16 KB page-size support on Play for newer target SDKs, and new arm64 devices are shipping 16 KB kernels. On those devices BOINC will install and show its UI, but it can never compute.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an emulator from a ps16k system image (for example google_apis_ps16k, x86_64)
2. Install any current BOINC Android build and launch it
3. The app stays on the splash screen; logcat shows the Monitor connect retries and the client process never appears in ps

### Expected behavior

The native client starts on 16 KB page-size devices the same way it does on 4 KB ones.

### Proposed fix

Link the Android client binaries with a 16 KB max page size by adding `-Wl,-z,max-page-size=16384` to the NDK link flags in the Android build scripts. Binaries aligned to 16 KB still load fine on 4 KB kernels, so this is backward compatible. The Android apps and wrapper builds will eventually want the same flag.

I have a fix in progress and will open a PR once I've rebuilt the client and verified both the alignment and the behavior on a ps16k image.

title: Android: link 64-bit client binaries with 16 KB page alignment
body:
Fixes #7194

**Description of the Change**

Adds `-Wl,-z,max-page-size=16384` to the link flags of the arm64 and x86_64 client builds, so the client binaries load on Android devices with 16 KB page-size kernels. Today they are linked with 4 KB ELF segment alignment (PT_LOAD align 0x1000 in the current CI binaries), which a 16 KB kernel refuses to load: the app UI runs but the native client silently never starts. Details and reproduction are in #7194.

16 KB aligned binaries remain fully compatible with 4 KB kernels, so nothing changes for existing devices. The 32-bit ABIs are unchanged since 16 KB page-size kernels only exist for 64-bit.

**Verification (all done)**

- [x] The CI artifacts from this PR's own Android run have PT_LOAD alignment 0x4000: verified by parsing the ELF program headers of the x86_64 and arm64-v8a client binaries from the run artifacts.
- [x] Runtime test on a 16 KB kernel (Android 15 google_apis_ps16k x86_64 emulator, getconf PAGE_SIZE confirms 16384): the current 4 KB aligned client reproducibly fails to start there (the Monitor loops on "not found in ps output"), and the same app repacked with this PR's CI-built client starts normally, the UI connects, and it keeps running with no errors.
- [x] Control on a standard 4 KB Android 14 (API 34) x86_64 emulator: the 16 KB aligned client starts and runs exactly like before, so no regression on existing devices.

**Alternate Designs**

Building separate 16 KB variants of the client was not considered seriously since a single 16 K aligned binary works on both page sizes. Adding the flag to the 32-bit ABIs too was considered and skipped as meaningless there, though it would be harmless.

**Release Notes**

Android: BOINC now works on devices with 16 KB memory page kernels.

title: Client: NVIDIA detection uses the deprecated cuDeviceComputeCapability API and aborts if it's missing
body:
### Describe the bug

The client reads GPU compute capability through cuDeviceComputeCapability (client/gpu_nvidia.cpp:419), which Nvidia deprecated years ago. Two problems with that:

- If the symbol is ever missing from the driver library, detection doesn't degrade, it aborts. The warning path at client/gpu_nvidia.cpp:352 gives up on all Nvidia GPUs, so the day Nvidia drops the deprecated symbol, clients lose GPU computing entirely instead of just falling back.
- The call's return value isn't checked, so a failed read silently leaves whatever was in the struct.

The modern replacement is cuDeviceGetAttribute with CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_COMPUTE_CAPABILITY_MAJOR/MINOR, and the client already binds cuDeviceGetAttribute for other attributes.

### Steps to reproduce

Not reproducible with current drivers (they still export the symbol). The abort path is at client/gpu_nvidia.cpp:352: if the lookup fails, detection jumps to the exit instead of continuing without the deprecated call.

### Expected behavior

Compute capability is read via cuDeviceGetAttribute, the deprecated call stays only as a fallback for old drivers, and a missing legacy symbol no longer disables all GPU detection.

title: Client: hosts with OpenCL-only NVIDIA detection report compute capability 0 to the scheduler
body:
### Describe the bug

When CUDA detection fails but OpenCL succeeds, correlate_opencl() backfills memory, clock and name from the OpenCL properties but not cuda_prop.major/minor (client/gpu_opencl.cpp:817). The scheduler request then carries `<major>0</major>`, so every server side compute capability check (min_nvidia_compcap and max_nvidia_compcap in plan_class_spec.cpp, the legacy cuda_check) sees 0 for these hosts.

The OpenCL reported values are already detected (nv_compute_capability_major/minor via the cl_nv_device_attribute_query extension) and are even used for peak flops estimation in COPROC_NVIDIA::set_peak_flops() (lib/coproc.cpp:564). They just never get copied into the fields that are serialized as `<major>/<minor>`.

### Expected behavior

On OpenCL-only hosts, cuda_prop.major/minor are backfilled from the OpenCL compute capability values, with CUDA values winning whenever present, matching the precedence set_peak_flops() already uses.

title: client: fixes to NVIDIA GPU detection
body: 1) The cuDeviceComputeCapability() function in the CUDA library was deprecated some time ago (2019?) and may be removed in the future. Currently CUDA GPU detection fails if this function is absent. Instead, use cuDeviceGetAttribute() instead. Fixes #7196 2) If we find an NVIDIA GPU via OpenCL and not CUDA, set its compute capability in the CUDA_DEVICE_PROP; that's what is used by the server plan-class logic. Fixes #7197 --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes NVIDIA GPU detection to work without the deprecated CUDA API and for OpenCL-only NVIDIA GPUs. title: Update ProjectProcessingPage.cpp
body: Fixes #6104 **Description of the Change** The root cause of was an unsafe cast of a member function pointer in the static event table: ```cpp EVT_PROJECTPROCESSING_STATECHANGE( CProjectProcessingPage::OnStateChange ) ``` This macro forced a cast from `void (CProjectProcessingPage::*)(CProjectProcessingPageEvent&)` to `wxEventFunction` (i.e., `void (wxEvtHandler::*)(wxEvent&)`), which is a cast between incompatible pointer types. Under GCC with `-Wcast-function-type`, this results in undefined behavior – the `this` pointer is misadjusted when the event handler is called, causing the state machine (`m_iCurrentState`, flags, and button enable/disable logic) to read/write garbage memory. Consequently, the wizard’s internal page history becomes corrupted, leading to the looping back behaviour and the back button never being greyed out. To fix this, the static event table entry for `wxEVT_PROJECTPROCESSING_STATECHANGE` has been removed and replaced with a type‑safe dynamic binding using `Bind()` in the `Create()` method. `Bind()` uses templates to correctly adjust the `this` pointer, eliminating the UB and the compiler warning. The other static entries (`EVT_WIZARDEX_PAGE_CHANGED` and `EVT_WIZARDEX_CANCEL`) are unchanged because they use compatible function signatures. After this change, the wizard’s state transitions work correctly, the back button follows the expected page history, and it becomes disabled when appropriate. Assisted-by: (not using an agent): DeepSeek-V4 **Alternate Designs** Keeping the static event table but modify the macro to use `wxDECLARE_EVENT_TABLE_ENTRY` with a proper functor that performs a safe cast. This would require changes in the header file and deeper understanding of wxWidgets’ internal event mechanism, making it more error‑prone and less maintainable. **Release Notes** Fixed erratic "Back" button behaviour in the project attach wizard (Linux builds from master). --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #6104 by replacing an unsafe static event handler with a type-safe `Bind()` for the state-change event. title: Update main.cpp
body: Fixes #1544 **Description of the Change** Reorder the initialization sequence in init_core_client() to ensure that command-line arguments correctly override settings from cc_config.xml. Before: command-line parsing happened before reading the config file, so XML values unconditionally overwrote the earlier command-line settings. After: 1. The --dir/-dir argument is extracted and handled early to change the working directory before any config file is read. 2. cc_config.defaults() and nvc_config.defaults() are called. 3. A first pass of gstate.parse_cmdline() parses all remaining arguments. 4. read_config_file(true) loads cc_config.xml from the now-correct working directory. 5. A second pass of gstate.parse_cmdline() re-applies all command-line options, which now take precedence over the XML-loaded values. This change also updates do_gpu_detection() to follow the same pattern (read config first, then parse command line), keeping behaviour consistent. Assisted-by: (not using an agent): DeepSeek-V4 **Alternate Designs** Two other approaches were considered: 1. Add source-tracking flags – extend CC_CONFIG with per-option set_by_cmdline booleans and skip XML assignment when that flag is true. This is more invasive, touches many configuration members, and increases maintenance overhead. 2. Swap only the order without handling --dir specially – but this would break if cc_config.xml is not in the current directory when the client starts, because the directory change would happen after reading the file. The chosen design is the simplest and least intrusive: it uses the existing parsing mechanism twice, requiring no changes to parse_options_client() or CC_CONFIG structure, and correctly handles directory changes. **Release Notes** Fix command-line options being overridden by `cc_config.xml`; command‑line arguments now take precedence over the configuration file. --- ## Summary by cubic Command-line arguments now correctly override cc_config.xml across platforms. init_core_client(): extract and apply `--dir` before first parse, switch to the data dir (or default on Windows), read config, then re-parse CLI to override; do_gpu_detection(): read config before CLI parse and remove the late read so diagnostics honor flags. title: client: don't use swap usage from state file
body: 8.2.15 and earlier clients used VM size as swap usage. In some cases this value was greater than swap space size. The client would then never schedule the job. Instead, ignore the value in the state file. The client will measure the swap usage (correctly) when it runs the job. Fixes #7146 --- ## Summary by cubic Ignore swap usage from the client state file to prevent false scheduling blocks. Previously the client used the saved swap value (often VM size), which could exceed actual swap space and keep tasks from ever running; now the state value is ignored and swap usage is measured when the task runs. - Removes parsing of the swap_size field in the state file; other state fields are unchanged. - No migration or config changes. Existing state files remain valid; their swap values are simply ignored. - Tasks previously blocked by inflated swap usage should now be scheduled and run. Written for commit 450b2ac89f0504a68aac58e64e73cdb387a4a9ce. Summary will update on new commits.

title: antique_file_deleter: stale errno from check_stop_daemons() misreported as a readdir() failure
body:
## Summary

`sched/antique_file_deleter.cpp`'s `delete_antiques_from_dir()` can log a false `Couldn't read dir '<path>': No such file or directory (2)` and abort the entire scan, even though the directory was read completely and successfully. This happens on essentially every *empty* upload fanout directory under completely normal, default settings -- i.e. routinely, for any project young enough (or with a large enough `uldl_dir_fanout`) that some fanout buckets are still empty.

## Root cause

`errno` is reset to `0` once, before the `while ((entry = readdir(dir)))` loop starts, but never again inside the loop. Each iteration calls `check_stop_daemons()` (`sched/sched_util_basic.cpp:71`), which calls `boinc_file_exists()` to check for a `stop_daemons` trigger file -- and correctly gets `ENOENT` when that file doesn't exist (the normal case). That leaves `errno == ENOENT` as a side effect that's never cleared.

For a directory containing only `.` and `..` (any empty directory), the loop body never reaches the later `lstat()` call (which does its own `errno = 0;` reset) because `.`/`..` entries hit `continue` immediately. So by the time `readdir()` genuinely returns `NULL` for real end-of-directory -- a normal, non-error condition that doesn't itself touch `errno` -- `errno` still holds the stale `ENOENT` from `check_stop_daemons()`. The post-loop check:

```cpp
// if the loop terminated because of an error
if (errno) {
    log_messages.printf(MSG_CRITICAL,
        "delete_antiques_from_dir(): "
        "Couldn't read dir '%s': %s (%d)\n",
        dirpath, strerror(errno), errno
    );
    closedir(dir);
    return 1;
}
```

sees that stale value and misreports a completely successful scan as a read failure.

## Confirmed via strace

Tracing a real run against an empty fanout directory:

```
getdents64(4, ..., 32768)                     = 48         # readdir() succeeds, 2 entries: "." ".."
newfstatat(AT_FDCWD, "./config.xml", ...)     = -1 ENOENT  # check_stop_daemons() -> config.project_path() probe
newfstatat(AT_FDCWD, "../config.xml", ...)    = 0
newfstatat(AT_FDCWD, "../cgi-bin", ...)       = 0
newfstatat(AT_FDCWD, "../stop_daemons", ...)  = -1 ENOENT  # boinc_file_exists(stop_daemons) -- this is what gets misreported
```

## Reproduction

1. A project with `<httpd_user>` set correctly and `<uldl_dir_fanout>` configured (any nonzero value).
2. No `stop_daemons` file present (the normal state).
3. At least one upload fanout subdirectory that's currently empty -- trivially true on a fresh project, or one still ramping up traffic.
4. Run `antique_file_deleter -d 2`.

Expected: silent success (or debug-level logging only).
Actual: `[CRITICAL] delete_antiques_from_dir(): Couldn't read dir '<upload>/<bucket>': No such file or directory (2)`, and the run aborts entirely -- `delete_antiques()`'s own loop over fanout buckets does `if (ret < 0) return ret;`, so every remaining bucket gets skipped too, not just the one that "failed."

## Suggested fix

Reset `errno` immediately before each individual `readdir()` call, not once before the whole loop, so a later syscall within the same iteration can't leak into the next iteration's error check:

```diff
-    // scan directory
-    errno = 0;
-    while ((entry = readdir(dir))) {
-
-        // might be woken by a signal
-        check_stop_daemons();
+    // scan directory
+    while (1) {
+        errno = 0;
+        entry = readdir(dir);
+        if (!entry) break;
+
+        // might be woken by a signal
+        check_stop_daemons();
```

## Environment

- BOINC commit `d498cd24c27462786977947f9d0315663fe46be9`
- Debian bookworm, MariaDB backend
- Reproduced on a real, low-traffic project's upload directory (1024-bucket fanout, most buckets still empty)

Happy to open a PR with this fix if useful.

---

_Diagnosis (strace trace, source analysis, and the suggested fix) was drafted with AI assistance (Claude Sonnet 5), per BOINC's AI assistant contribution policy. The fix was compiled and run against a real production BOINC deployment before this report was written, and I've reviewed and confirm the analysis above myself._

title: RFC: Opt-in P2P Data Distribution Layer using libp2p/IPFS CIDs (Addressing the Bandwidth Bottleneck)
body:
### Describe the problem

As we know, server bandwidth costs and the `thundering herd` problem during large **WU** batch releases remain significant pain points for many BOINC projects (especially data-heavy ones like Climateprediction.net or Rosetta).

I am aware of the historical attempts to solve this, notably BT-BOINC (BitTorrent) in 2008, which was ultimately rejected due to:

- Security risks (Poisoning)
- UX nightmares (NAT/Port Forwarding requirements)
- Availability issues (Hanging at 99% when seeders drop)


### Describe the solution you'd like

I am a Software engineer and a BOINC [veteran](https://www.worldcommunitygrid.org/getDynamicImage.do?memberName=xclubx&mnOn=true&stat=3&imageNum=1&rankOn=true&projectsOn=false&special=true&link=0&memberId=808402) (~14 years, Top-3k). I am preparing to build a modern, lightweight P2P overlay for BOINC. We can now solve all the 2008 issues using modern protocols (libp2p, Trustless IPFS Gateways, and CIDs) without altering the user experience.

**How it works (Zero-Breakage Architecture)**

- Server-side: BOINC servers do not need to run full IPFS nodes. The server only needs to hash files (e.g., BLAKE3/IPLD) and inject an `<ipfs_cid>` tag into the WU XML `<file_info>`. Old clients will safely ignore this tag.

- Client-side: We introduce an opt-in C++ wrapper (leveraging rust-libp2p via FFI) into HTTP_OP. If the client sees `<ipfs_cid>`, it attempts to fetch the file via the P2P swarm.

- NAT Traversal: Modern libp2p handles NAT automatically via Circuit Relay v2 (UDP hole punching). No user configuration is required.

- Graceful Fallback: If the swarm lacks the file or times out (e.g., >5 seconds), the client seamlessly falls back to standard HTTP via the legacy `<url>` tag.

- Security: CIDs are cryptographically secure (Merkle DAGs). Any poisoned block is rejected on the fly before reaching the BOINC signature validation step.

**The Roadmap & Proof of Concept**
I do not expect this to be merged blindly. My plan is to conduct a controlled Pilot Study first:

- Develop the C++ FFI wrapper in a custom fork.

- Partner with an opt-in beta community (e.g., specific project power-users) running this custom client.

- Collect telemetry and publish a Case Study proving the actual egress reduction (targeting >40%) and stability.


**Questions for the Core Team**

- Are there any conceptual blockers for adding an optional `<ipfs_cid>` tag to the XML parser, provided it's strictly ignored by older clients?

- If the independent Pilot Study successfully proves the egress reduction and zero-breakage fallback, would you be open to reviewing the PR for mainline inclusion?

### Additional context

**My Commitment & Infrastructure**

To ensure this isn't just a "hit-and-run" PR, I am securing an infrastructure grant focused on Decentralized Science (DeSci) and Open Data. This funding covers my dedicated R&D time to maintain this integration long-term.
Furthermore, it fully covers the OpEx for an enterprise-grade bare-metal server (~20TB storage, high-throughput channel). 
This server will act as the primary Bootstrap/Relay node for the swarm, guaranteeing it remains 100% free and highly available for the BOINC community during the pilot and beyond.

title: LODA version: 2608.01 memory leak
body: ### Describe the bug LODA 2608.01 has a memory leak. Multiple tasks accumulated 1+ GB each over several hours, driving a 16 GB machine to 56 MB free. At that point Windows couldn't allocate GPU render buffers → browser images broken, BOINC UI blank, Snip Tool blank, PowerShell layout garbled. Active TCP sessions (RDP, VSCode Claude Code API call) got corrupted. Only ICMP (ping) kept working since it's kernel-level. ``` PS C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0> Write-Host "=== Physical RAM ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan === Physical RAM === PS C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0> Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem | >> Select-Object @{N="Total_GB";E={[math]::Round($_.TotalVisibleMemorySize/1MB,1)}}, >> @{N="Free_GB";E={[math]::Round($_.FreePhysicalMemory/1MB,1)}} >> Total_GB Free_GB -------- ------- 15.8 0.9 ``` Task was running over 27 hrs wu_1787932787_10809_0 — Elapsed: 1d 07:10:41 — still Running Fixes applied: BOINC snoozed → LODA killed → WSL2 shutdown → 6 GB freed → everything recovered except the VSCode instance with the hung API call, which needed an extension host reset. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Run multiple LODA 2608.01 tasks via BOINC on Windows 10 (16 GB RAM) 2. Let tasks run for 3+ hours 3. Observe loda-260801-windows-x86.exe processes growing continuously in memory 4. After ~3 hours, individual processes reach 1+ GB each (expected: <50 MB for a math search task) 5. With 13 concurrent tasks running, total LODA memory consumption drove a 16 GB machine to 56 MB free Work units affected: wu_1787932787_10771_0 wu_1787932787_10791_0 wu_1787932787_10787_0 wu_1787932787_10779_0 wu_1787932787_10772_0 wu_1787932787_10788_0 wu_1787932787_9248_1 wu_1787932787_9275_1 wu_1787932787_10809_0 ← longest running, 1d 07:10:41 elapsed wu_1787932787_10786_0 wu_1787932787_9185_1 wu_1787932787_10810_0 wu_1787932787_10780_0 wu_1787932787_9188_1 wu_1787932787_9183_1 OS: Windows 10 RAM: 16 GB BOINC version: check yours under Help > About ### Expected behavior Stable memory usage throughout task runtime loda-260801-windows-x86.exe processes maintain stable, bounded memory usage throughout the duration of a task. For a mathematical sequence search workload, memory usage should remain well under 100 MB per process regardless of runtime. Actual behaviour: Continuous memory growth, no upper bound ### Screenshots Sorry i dont have more detailed view, but notice RESMON memory tab, memory chalk full. ### System information Windows 10 fully updated Boinc 8.2.11 x64 ### Additional context - Peak observed: single loda-260801-windows-x86.exe process at 1.6 GB Working Set - 13 concurrent LODA tasks consumed enough RAM to bring a 16 GB system to 56 MB free - The longest-running task (wu_1787932787_10809_0) had elapsed 1d 07:10:41 at time of observation - Memory grew continuously with no plateau — the leak does not appear to self-limit - Side effects of full RAM exhaustion on the host machine included: browser rendering failures, RDP session corruption, GUI rendering failures across unrelated applications (BOINC Manager UI, Windows Snip Tool), and VSCode extension host becoming unresponsive - LODA is already set to "Won't get new tasks, Will remove when tasks done" on this machine — these were existing tasks completing, not new ones - Killing the loda processes and freeing RAM resolved all symptoms immediately - BOINC Computing Preferences RAM cap is recommended as a workaround until fixed

title: SUSE 16 rpm: bundled /etc/init.d/boinc-client makes systemctl enable fail — %post errors and the service is never enabled (Leap 16 removed systemd-sysv-install)
body:
## Environment

- openSUSE Leap 16.0 (x86_64)
- First hit with `boinc-client-8.2.9-4096.x86_64` from the repo
  `https://boinc.berkeley.edu/dl/linux/stable/suse16_0`
- **Current stable is affected too**: the 8.2.15 release asset
  `boinc-client-8.2.15-4612.x86_64_suse16_0.rpm`
  (from https://github.com/BOINC/boinc/releases/tag/client_release%2F8.2%2F8.2.15) also ships
  `/etc/init.d/boinc-client` (verified with `rpm -qpl`), and upgrading to it reinstates the file.

## Symptom

`zypper install boinc-client` reports success, but the `%post` scriptlet fails and the systemd
service is left **disabled**. From `/var/log/zypp/history`:

```
# Synchronizing state of boinc-client.service with SysV service script with /usr/lib/systemd/systemd-sysv-install.
# Executing: /usr/lib/systemd/systemd-sysv-install enable boinc-client
# warning: %post(boinc-client-8.2.9-4096.x86_64) scriptlet failed, exit status 1
```

Any later manual attempt fails the same way, and the enable symlink is never created:

```
$ sudo systemctl enable --now boinc-client.service
Synchronizing state of boinc-client.service with SysV service script with /usr/lib/systemd/systemd-sysv-install.
Executing: /usr/lib/systemd/systemd-sysv-install enable boinc-client
Failed to execute /usr/lib/systemd/systemd-sysv-install: No such file or directory
$ systemctl is-enabled boinc-client.service
disabled
```

Net effect: the install *looks* fine, `systemctl start` works for the current boot, and the user
discovers a dead client after the next reboot.

## Root cause

The rpm ships a SysV init script at `/etc/init.d/boinc-client` (installed mode 0644, so it could
never run as an init script anyway) alongside the native `boinc-client.service` unit. When an
init script matching the unit name exists, `systemctl enable` also synchronizes SysV state via
the distro helper `/usr/lib/systemd/systemd-sysv-install` — and openSUSE Leap 16 **removed that
helper entirely** (no package provides it; SysV compat is gone). systemctl then aborts the whole
enable operation, native symlink included.

Verified root cause, not a guess: after `sudo rm /etc/init.d/boinc-client`,
`systemctl enable --now boinc-client.service` succeeds immediately
(`Created symlink /etc/systemd/system/multi-user.target.wants/boinc-client.service ...`) and the
client runs normally (13 projects, CPU + CUDA/OpenCL GPU work).

## Suggested fix

Don't install the SysV script on systemd-enabled targets. The package already ships a native
`boinc-client.service`, so the init script adds nothing there — and every rpm target currently
built (`fc43`, `fc44`, `suse16_0`) is a systemd-native distribution. On SUSE 16 it has gone from
dead weight to actively harmful: its mere presence in `/etc/init.d/` is what routes
`systemctl enable` into the removed compat helper.

Making `%post` tolerate the sync failure would hide the install-time error but still leave every
future `systemctl disable/enable` cycle broken for users — not shipping the script on systemd
targets is the real fix.

## Workaround for affected users

```
sudo rm /etc/init.d/boinc-client
sudo systemctl enable --now boinc-client.service
```

(The file returns on every package upgrade; enabled state persists, so it only bites again on a
future disable/enable.)

title: send_email() crashes with an uncaught fatal error on any real SMTP failure (missing PHPMailer\PHPMailer\Exception require)
validate_email_addr.php, delete_account_request.php, edit_email_action.php, team_founder_transfer_action.php don't check send_email()'s return value
body:
\`send_email()\` returns \`false\` on failure, and several pages that depend on it ignore that return value and unconditionally show a success message:

- \`html/user/validate_email_addr.php\`'s \`send_validate_email()\` — always shows "An email has been sent to you," even on a failed send.
- \`html/user/delete_account_request.php\`'s \`delete_account_request_action()\` — always shows "Confirmation Email Sent." This one's the most consequential: the confirmation link is the only way to delete an account, so a silent failure here blocks the feature with zero indication anything went wrong.
- \`html/user/edit_email_action.php\` — the address change itself succeeds (correctly), but the page never says whether the two notice emails (to the old and new address) failed.
- \`html/user/team_founder_transfer_action.php\` — both the \`initiate_transfer\` and \`decline\` branches claim the other party was notified "by email" regardless of whether the send actually worked.

**Suggested fix:** check \`send_email()\`'s return value at each call site and show an honest failure message. The underlying action (DB update, PM, etc.) should stay non-blocking either way — only the message needs to be accurate.

Happy to open a PR with all four.

body:
Unrelated to each other and to #7277/#7278/#7279, found incidentally in adjacent code:

- **\`html/inc/forum.inc\`, \`move_thread()\`** — \`posts\` is decremented with no floor, unlike \`threads\` right next to it in the same query (\`threads=if(threads>0, threads-1, 0)\` vs. bare \`posts=posts-$thread->replies-1\`), so it can go negative.
- **\`html/inc/forum.inc\`, \`check_banished()\`** — shows only a bare date (\`gmdate('M j, Y', ...)\`) for a posting suspension, with no time and no timezone label — for any suspension under 48 hours (most of \`manage_user.php\`'s own duration options), this is close to meaningless ("you may not post until today"). Also, once a time is added, it needs an explicit timezone label (e.g. via the project's own \`time_str()\` helper) since a bare time looks like local time but is UTC.
- **\`html/inc/forum_email.inc\`, \`send_thread_moderation_email()\`** — references \`$action\`, an undefined variable (the function's actual parameter is \`$action_name\`), producing a garbled email subject line and a PHP warning.
- **\`html/inc/team.inc\`, \`new_member_list()\`** and **\`html/user/team_delta.php\`, \`show_delta()\`** — both call \`BoincUser::lookup_id()\` without checking for a null result, crashing with "Attempt to read property on null" if a user who joined/left a team, or appears in its change history, has since been deleted.
- **\`html/inc/news.inc\`, \`show_news()\`** — assumes every non-hidden thread in the News forum has at least one post, which isn't guaranteed once a thread's only post can be moved elsewhere via post-moderation; crashes instead of skipping the empty thread.
- **\`html/user/friend.php\`** (\`html/inc/friend.inc\`) — \`send_friend_request_email()\`/\`send_friend_accept_email()\` call \`strlen($msg)\` where \`$msg\` can be \`null\` (no message typed), triggering a PHP 8.1 deprecation notice.
- **\`html/user/forum_banishment_vote_action.php\`** — never calls \`page_head()\`/\`page_tail()\` at all, so its response is permanently a bare, unstyled page with no HTML structure, regardless of outcome. Separately, its reason-category \`switch\` has no \`break;\` statements so every case falls through to \`"Other"\` — though this currently has no visible effect, since \`start_vote()\` never actually uses the category value at all.

Happy to open a PR with fixes for all of these.

---

*This report (investigation, diagnosis, and suggested fix) was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Sonnet 5). All findings were verified against the actual BOINC source and, where noted above, reproduced live against a running test deployment. Any resulting PR will include the required `Assisted-by:` trailer per the BOINC AI Assistants Usage Policy.*

title: lib: add FreeBSD-native process enumeration and total CPU time
body: - Add a `__FreeBSD__` branch to `procinfo_setup()` that uses `sysctl(CTL_KERN, KERN_PROC, KERN_PROC_PROC)` to populate `PROCINFO` from `struct kinfo_proc (ki_pid, ki_ppid, ki_comm, ki_rusage, ki_rssize, ki_nice)`, instead of walking `/proc`. - Add a `__FreeBSD__` branch to `total_cpu_time()` that reads the `kern.cp_time` sysctl, scaled by` kern.clockrate`'s `stathz`, instead of parsing `/proc/stat`. - Include `lib/util.h` for `PROCESS_IDLE_PRIORITY`. Assisted-by: Claude:claude-sonnet-5 [web_search] [web_fetch] Assisted-by: ChatGPT:GPT-5.6 Luna Fixes # — no existing issue. On FreeBSD, `procinfo_setup()` and `total_cpu_time()` fall through to the Linux-format `/proc` parsing path unconditionally, since it's currently written to run for "any non-Solaris Unix." FreeBSD has no `/proc` by default inside jails, so in these cases, `procinfo_setup()` fails outright (`procinfo_setup(): can't open /proc`, visible in client logs) and CPU-load-based task suspension does not function. Separately, even where a Linux-compatible `/proc` is made available (via `linprocfs`), a per-process approach run inside a FreeBSD jail can only ever observe that jail's own process table by design — never sibling jails' or the host's CPU load — so it cannot deliver correct suspend/resume behavior for the common deployment pattern of running `boinc-client` in an isolated jail alongside other jailed or host-level workloads. **Description of the Change** Adds a native FreeBSD branch to `procinfo_setup()` using `sysctl(CTL_KERN, KERN_PROC, KERN_PROC_PROC)`, reading `struct kinfo_proc` directly instead of walking `/proc/PID/stat`; this is naturally scoped by the kernel to whatever the calling jail can see, matching the existing behavior of `ps`/`top` inside a jail, and is exactly the correct process set for "BOINC-related processes" since BOINC only ever runs inside its own jail. Adds a native FreeBSD branch to `total_cpu_time()` using the `kern.cp_time` sysctl, scaled by `kern.clockrate`'s `stathz`; unlike a per-process walk, this is a host-wide kernel counter unaffected by jail process-visibility restrictions, giving an accurate "how busy is the whole machine" signal from inside a jail with no special configuration required. Together these give correct CPU-load-based suspension covering sibling jails and the host, not just the calling jail. Tested on FreeBSD 14.3/amd64: confirmed BOINC-driven computation correctly suspends when non-jailed CPU load is introduced from outside the BOINC jail, and resumes when that load is removed. This method also functions properly when BOINC is run on bare metal. **Alternate Designs** - Mount `linprocfs` at `/proc` inside the BOINC jail and rely on the existing Linux-format-parsing code path unmodified. Rejected: per-process enumeration inside a jail can only ever see that jail's own processes by design — a hard security boundary, not a configuration gap — so this can never observe sibling-jail or host-level CPU load regardless of `/proc` availability, and does not solve the underlying problem. - Use `libkvm` instead of `sysctl(KERN_PROC_PROC`) for process enumeration. Not pursued: `libkvm` typically requires additional privileges (e.g. `kmem` group membership) that a raw `sysctl` call does not, with no capability advantage for the fields needed here (pid, ppid, command, rusage, rss, nice), all available directly via `struct kinfo_proc`. **Release Notes** Added native FreeBSD support for CPU-load-based task suspension, so `boinc-client` running inside a FreeBSD jail correctly responds to CPU demand from sibling jails and the host, not just from within its own jail. --- ## Summary by cubic Replaces `/proc`-based process and CPU time reading on FreeBSD with native sysctl calls so CPU-load suspension works inside jails and without a procfs mount. Previously the code fell through to the Linux `/proc` parsing path, which fails outright in FreeBSD jails (no `/proc` by default) and, even with `linprocfs`, only sees the jail's own processes, so host and sibling-jail CPU load never triggered suspension. **Bug Fixes** - Process enumeration now uses `sysctl(CTL_KERN, KERN_PROC, KERN_PROC_PROC)` instead of walking `/proc`. - Total CPU time reads `kern.cp_time`, a host-wide counter unaffected by jail process-visibility restrictions. - Enables the improved `non_boinc_cpu_usage` calculation on FreeBSD by adding it to the conditional compile guard. Written for commit 0169e330b5a41c63ab13be7d6aca4ad2d8db284e. Summary will update on new commits.

title: client: fix register clobber and expand FreeBSD CPU feature detection
body: In `use_cpuid(`) (FreeBSD, i386/amd64): - Fix vendor-string extraction: copy the leaf-0 vendor bytes out of `p[]` before calling `do_cpuid(0x1, p)`, which otherwise overwrites them first. - Initialize `cpu_id` to silence `-Wsometimes-uninitialized`. - Gate AVX/AVX2 detection on XSAVE + OSXSAVE + `XGETBV(0)` rather than the raw `CPUID` bit alone. - Expand feature detection from 7 flags to the full leaf 1 EDX/ECX, leaf 0x80000001 EDX/ECX (vendor-gated Intel/AMD/Hygon bits), and leaf 7 sub-leaf 0 EBX set, using canonical token names matching `parse_cpuinfo_linux()`. Assisted-by: Claude:claude-sonnet-5 [web_search] [web_fetch] Assisted-by: ChatGPT:GPT-5.6 Luna Fixes unreported issue. On FreeBSD, `use_cpuid()` copies the CPU vendor string out of `p[]` after a second `do_cpuid()` call has already overwritten that buffer with unrelated register contents, so `p_vendor` is populated from stale/wrong data. On hardware where the clobbering leaf-1 EBX value happens to start with a null byte (confirmed on an Intel Atom C2550 under FreeBSD 14.3), this produces an empty `p_vendor`. Observed downstream effect: at least one BOINC project (NFS@Home) responds to scheduler requests from an otherwise fully functional FreeBSD host with "Missing CPU type in request." **Description of the Change** Fixes the ordering bug by copying the leaf-0 vendor bytes before the leaf-1 call that clobbers them. While auditing this function, two related issues were also addressed: AVX/AVX2 detection previously trusted the raw CPUID bit without confirming OSXSAVE and OS-level YMM-state support via XGETBV, which can misreport AVX availability to science apps that then crash executing AVX instructions; and feature detection covered only 7 flags total, versus roughly 60 already reported on Windows and Linux for the same hardware, meaning FreeBSD hosts were systematically excluded from optimized app versions available to every other platform. All three are fixed together since they live in the same function and were found during the same audit; token spelling for the newly added flags matches `parse_cpuinfo_linux()`'s canonical names for cross-platform `plan_class` consistency. Verified bit-for-bit against `dmesg`-reported CPUID feature masks on real Intel hardware; AMD/Hygon-specific and AVX2/BMI code paths are verified by inspection only, not yet exercised on hardware that sets those bits. This PR does not add aarch64 support — use_cpuid() remains correctly guarded to `__i386__`/`__amd64__` only, since ARM64 has no equivalent instruction or register layout; FreeBSD/aarch64 continues to fall through to the existing generic `sysctl(HW_MACHINE/HW_MODEL)` path unchanged. **Alternate Designs** - Fix the existing `LINUX_LIKE_SYSTEM` macro so FreeBSD parses `/proc/cpuinfo` the way Linux does. Rejected: `LINUX_LIKE_SYSTEM` would then need to be unconditionally true on every FreeBSD build regardless of whether a Linux-compatible `/proc` exists, causing every FreeBSD client without a Linux compatibility layer — the large majority — to attempt and fail to open a Linux-format `/proc`, for no benefit: the fields this would supply are already available natively via `use_cpuid()` and existing `sysctlbyname()` calls elsewhere in this file. - A shared, table-driven (leaf, register, bit) -> name decoder consumed by both hostinfo_win.cpp and hostinfo_unix.cpp, to prevent this class of naming-duplication bug (will be submitting a companion Windows typo PR) at the source. Deferred to a separate, smaller follow-up rather than bundled here, since it would touch two platforms' code in a single change. **Release Notes** Fixed a bug on FreeBSD causing the CPU vendor field to frequently report empty, which could cause some projects to reject work requests from FreeBSD hosts; also expanded FreeBSD CPU feature reporting to match Linux and Windows. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes a FreeBSD-only bug in `use_cpuid()` where a later CPUID call overwrote the CPU vendor string, causing empty vendor fields that led projects like NFS@Home to reject work requests. The function now also reports the full CPU feature set like Linux and Windows, and only claims AVX/AVX2 when the OS actually supports it. **Bug Fixes** - Copies vendor bytes out before the leaf-1 call that would overwrite them. - AVX/AVX2 require XSAVE, OSXSAVE, and XGETBV confirming OS-level YMM state. - Queries leaf 7 with an explicit sub-leaf via a new `bsd_cpuid_count()` helper, since `do_cpuid()` doesn't constrain ECX. - Initializes `cpu_id` to silence `-Wsometimes-uninitialized`. **New Features** - Expands reporting from 7 flags to leaves 1, 0x80000001, and 7 using `parse_cpuinfo_linux()` token names for consistent `plan_class`. - Grows the capabilities buffer from 256 to 1024 bytes. - AMD/Hygon and AVX2/BMI paths are verified by inspection only. - No aarch64 change; `use_cpuid()` remains guarded to `__i386__`/`__amd64__`. Written for commit 1e842f7302c007dc12e4db677d33e9a634076f7d. Summary will update on new commits.

title: client: fix CPU feature-name typos in Windows get_processor_features()
body: Correct three feature-name string literals: - "movebe" -> "movbe" - "page1gb" -> "pdpe1gb" - "topx" -> "topoext" Also add a trailing space after "rdrand" for consistency with the rest of the function. No change to which CPUID bits are tested. Assisted-by: Claude:claude-sonnet-5 [web_search] [web_fetch] Assisted-by: ChatGPT:GPT-5.6 Luna Fixes unreported issue. Three feature-name strings written by `get_processor_features()` on Windows don't match the canonical names BOINC uses elsewhere (`movebe` vs. `movbe`, `page1gb` vs. `pdpe1gb`, `topx` vs. `topoext`). Since `plan_class` project logic matches `p_features` with substring checks, these typos cause silent, unreported mismatches on Windows hosts specifically — a rule written against `movbe`, `pdpe1gb`, or `topoext` never matches on Windows even when the underlying CPUID bit is set, with no error surfaced anywhere. **Description of the Change** The canonical spelling for CPU feature tokens comes from Linux's `/proc/cpuinfo` `flags` line, which BOINC's `parse_cpuinfo_linux()` passes through verbatim from the kernel, and which is what existing project `plan_class` rules are written against. This PR brings the three mismatched Windows strings in line with that spelling, and adds a trailing space after `rdrand` for consistency with every other entry in the function. This is a pure string-literal correction — no change to which CPUID bits are tested or to control flow. **Alternate Designs** - Teach project-side `plan_class` parsers to recognize the Windows-specific spellings as aliases. Rejected: this pushes a client-side bug onto every project maintainer indefinitely, and the incorrect spellings aren't documented anywhere as an intentional convention worth aliasing against. - Rename all platforms' tokens to Intel SDM instruction-set naming instead of Linux kernel naming. Rejected: Linux's spelling is already what most existing `plan_class` rules are written against, since it's what the largest share of BOINC hosts report; introducing a third naming convention would create a new mismatch rather than resolving the existing one. **Release Notes** Fixed three CPU feature-name typos on Windows (`movebe`, `page1gb`, `topx`). --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes three CPU feature-name typos in Windows `get_processor_features()` so feature strings match the canonical names used in Linux and in `plan_class` rules. - Corrects `"movebe"` to `"movbe"`, `"page1gb"` to `"pdpe1gb"`, and `"topx"` to `"topoext"` on Windows hosts. - Adds a trailing space after `"rdrand"` for consistency with the other feature strings. No CPUID bits tested are changed. Written for commit f6efff98dcbab28a29323b491816e7ebd8d07316. Summary will update on new commits.

title: Add missing Exception.php require in send_email()
body: Closes #7277. `send_email()` requires `PHPMailer.php` and `SMTP.php` but never `Exception.php`, even though all three are part of the vendored PHPMailer library. This is invisible on the happy path — `PHPMailer\PHPMailer\Exception` is only touched when `smtpConnect()`/`smtpSend()`/`postSend()` hit a real connection or auth failure and try to throw it. Since the class was never loaded, PHP can't construct it, so instead of a catchable exception (which PHPMailer's own code turns into a clean `Send()` returning `false`), you get an uncaught fatal `Error` that crashes the whole request. Tested against a live deployment with a deliberately-broken SMTP password: before this change, a failed send crashes with `Class "PHPMailer\PHPMailer\Exception" not found`; after, `send_email()` returns `false` as intended. --- *Assisted by AI (Claude Sonnet 5) per the BOINC AI Assistants Usage Policy — see the commit's `Assisted-by:` trailer.* --- ## Summary by cubic `send_email()` no longer crashes with an uncaught `Class "PHPMailer\PHPMailer\Exception" not found` error on real SMTP connection or auth failures; it now requires `Exception.php` alongside `PHPMailer.php` and `SMTP.php` and returns `false` as intended. SMTP error details are now written to the error log via `error_log()` instead of being echoed to end users. Closes #7277. Written for commit 6217599ee5b2d16a33b4a7d5a7578952ed1bcf27. Summary will update on new commits.

title: Check send_email()'s return value in 4 account-flow pages
body: Closes #7278. `send_email()` returns `false` on failure, but these pages ignore that return value and unconditionally show a success message: - `validate_email_addr.php`'s `send_validate_email()` — always shows "An email has been sent to you." - `delete_account_request.php`'s `delete_account_request_action()` — always shows "Confirmation Email Sent." This one's the most consequential: the confirmation link is the only way to delete an account, so a silent failure blocked the feature with zero indication anything went wrong. - `edit_email_action.php` — the address change itself succeeds (correctly, unchanged here), but the page never said whether the two notice emails (old + new address) failed. - `team_founder_transfer_action.php` — both the `initiate_transfer` and `decline` branches claimed the other party was notified "by email" regardless of whether the send actually worked. Each fix checks the return value and shows an honest message on failure; the underlying action (DB update, PM, etc.) stays non-blocking either way — only the message changes. `validate_email_addr.php`/`delete_account_request.php` also had `page_head()` called only after the send, so a failure's raw `echo $mail->ErrorInfo` (from inside `send_email()`) landed before any ``/stylesheet output and broke the page's CSS. Moved `page_head()` before the send in both. Tested against a live deployment with SMTP deliberately broken: each page now shows the correct failure message instead of a false success, with CSS intact. --- *Assisted by AI (Claude Sonnet 5) per the BOINC AI Assistants Usage Policy — see the commit's `Assisted-by:` trailer.* --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes four account-flow pages that claimed an email was sent even when `send_email()` failed. - `delete_account_request.php` is the most consequential: the confirmation email is the only way to delete an account, so a silent failure blocked the feature with no indication. - `validate_email_addr.php` and `delete_account_request.php` now call `page_head()` before sending, so a failed send no longer prints raw error output before the stylesheet and breaks page CSS. - `edit_email_action.php` and `team_founder_transfer_action.php` now report when the notice emails failed to send; the underlying action (email address change, transfer request/decline) stays non-blocking. Written for commit 434204e6b38186c1a3cc7a6f11178960714fec65. Summary will update on new commits.

title: Don't hide moderation-email failures inside a 302 redirect body
body:
Closes #7279.

Both files called their respective notification-email function and then immediately `header('Location: ...')`, with nothing printed first:

```php
send_thread_moderation_email($forum, $thread, $reason, $action_name, $explanation);
header('Location: forum_thread.php?id='.$thread->id);
```

Since nothing is output before the redirect, `header()` always succeeds — but if the send failed, `send_email()`'s own `echo $mail->ErrorInfo` still produced output, which ends up as the body of the 302 response. Browsers never render a redirect's body, they just follow `Location:`, so the moderator sees a completely normal-looking redirect with zero indication the notification email failed. Confirmed by capturing the actual POST request and replaying it with `curl -i` (no `-L`): the raw SMTP error text is genuinely present in the 302 response body, just never shown by any browser.

Fix: buffer the send with `ob_start()`/`ob_get_clean()`, then redirect cleanly on success or render a real page with the captured output on failure. The moderation action itself already succeeded before this point either way and is never rolled back. Any dynamic text rendered on the failure page (`$email_output`, `$action_name`) is HTML-escaped.

**Edit:** this PR originally also changed `forum_moderate_thread_action.php` to only send the notification when a reason was given, based on a misreading of the "Reason (Mailed if nonempty)" label as gating the whole send. It doesn't — that label describes `$explanation` (built separately, from the same field) conditionally including the reason *text*; the notification itself should always go out. That change has been reverted (see the commit history and review thread below) — the notification is unconditional again, matching original behavior.

Tested against a live deployment with SMTP deliberately broken: before, a failed send's error was invisible inside the redirect; after, a real "Moderation notice" page shows the failure and the raw error text, CSS intact.

---

title: forum.inc: floor posts count in move_thread(), use time_str() in check_banished()
body: Fixes two independent bugs reported in #7280: - `move_thread()`: `posts` was decremented with no floor, unlike `threads` right next to it in the same query, so it can go negative. Clamped the same way `threads` already is. - `check_banished()`: showed only a bare date (`gmdate('M j, Y', ...)`) for a posting suspension, with no time and no timezone label. For any suspension under 48 hours (most of `manage_user.php`'s own duration options), this is close to meaningless. Switched to `time_str()`, the project's own standard helper used elsewhere for exactly this, which includes the time and an explicit UTC label. Both confirmed live on a running test deployment. --- *Assisted by AI (Claude Sonnet 5) per the BOINC AI Assistants Usage Policy — see the commit's `Assisted-by:` trailer.* --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes two forum bugs reported in #7280: moving a thread could drive the source forum's `posts` count negative, and ban notices showed only a bare date with no time or timezone. - Floors the `posts` decrement at 0, matching the existing `threads` handling in the same query. - Replaces the `gmdate()` call in `check_banished()` with `time_str()`, adding the time and an explicit UTC label so short suspensions under 48 hours are meaningful. title: team.inc, team_delta.php: guard BoincUser::lookup_id() against a deleted user
body: Fixes a bug reported in #7280: both `new_member_list()` (`team.inc`) and `show_delta()` (`team_delta.php`) call `BoincUser::lookup_id()` without checking for a null result, crashing with "Attempt to read property on null" if a user who joined/left a team, or appears in its change history, has since been deleted. - `new_member_list()`: added a null check before dereferencing, same as other unguarded lookups already handle elsewhere in this codebase. - `show_delta()`: this is an audit/history log, so the entry is kept (falling back to `$delta->userid`/"(deleted user)") rather than silently dropped. Both confirmed live on a running test deployment. --- *Assisted by AI (Claude Sonnet 5) per the BOINC AI Assistants Usage Policy — see the commit's `Assisted-by:` trailer.* --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes a crash in team member lists and team change history when a user has been deleted since the event occurred. `new_member_list()` now skips deleted users instead of crashing, and `show_delta()` keeps the audit entry, falling back to the stored user ID and "(deleted user)" for the name. title: friend.inc: avoid strlen(null) deprecation notice on PHP 8.1
body: Fixes a bug reported in #7280: `send_friend_request_email()`/`send_friend_accept_email()` call `strlen($msg)` where `$msg` can be `null` (no message typed), triggering a PHP 8.1 deprecation notice. A plain truthy check is null-safe and equivalent here (empty string and null both skip the block, same as before). Confirmed live on a running test deployment. --- *Assisted by AI (Claude Sonnet 5) per the BOINC AI Assistants Usage Policy — see the commit's `Assisted-by:` trailer.* --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes the PHP 8.1 deprecation notice reported in #7280 that appeared when sending friend request or acceptance emails with no message. The explicit null/empty-string check replaces `strlen($msg)` and skips the message block for both `null` and `''`, matching the previous behavior. Written for commit e764b0253e628927150e87ee0f652ef889d94e8a. Summary will update on new commits.

title: news.inc: skip threads with no posts in show_news()
body: Fixes a bug reported in #7280: `show_news()` assumed every non-hidden thread in the News forum has at least one post, which isn't guaranteed once a thread's only post can be moved elsewhere or deleted via post-level moderation (`forum_moderate_post_action.php`'s "move"/"delete" actions), leaving the thread itself intact but empty. `BoincPost::enum()` then returns an empty array, and dereferencing `$posts[0]` crashes with "Attempt to read property on null" here and in `news_item()`. Skips the thread instead of crashing. Confirmed live on a running test deployment (a real side effect of testing post moderation). --- *Assisted by AI (Claude Sonnet 5) per the BOINC AI Assistants Usage Policy — see the commit's `Assisted-by:` trailer.* --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #7280: `show_news()` crashed when a News forum thread had no posts, which can happen when post-level moderation moves or deletes the only post, leaving the thread empty. It now skips empty threads instead of trying to read the first post. Written for commit 7965f762ba6bfb0f4215c65d97654bb6425acb88. Summary will update on new commits.

title: forum_email.inc: fix undefined $action in send_thread_moderation_email()
body: Fixes a bug reported in #7280: `send_thread_moderation_email()` referenced `$action`, an undefined variable — the function's actual parameter is `$action_name`. title: Two team-admin actions crash under STRICT_TRANS_TABLES (missing NOT NULL column values on INSERT)
body:
Found two independent instances of the same bug class while testing team functionality on a project running MariaDB in `STRICT_TRANS_TABLES` mode (MariaDB's own modern default):

- **`html/user/team_forum.php`, `create_forum()`** — the INSERT only sets `category`/`parent_type`, but `forum.orderID`/`title`/`description` are all `NOT NULL` with no default. Silently fine under a lenient SQL mode (implicitly inserts `0`/`''`/`''`), but throws an uncaught `mysqli_sql_exception` ("Field '<col>' doesn't have a default value") under strict mode — crashes on creating a team's message board. Confirmed live: fixing `orderID` alone still crashes on `title` next, then `description`.
- **`html/user/team_admins.php`, `add_admin()`** — same class: the INSERT never sets `rights`, and `team_admin.rights` is `NOT NULL` with no default. Same crash when adding a team admin by email.

Both confirmed present verbatim at current `master`. Suggested fix for each: supply an explicit value for the missing column(s) — `0`/`''`/`''` for `team_forum.php` (an empty title/description is intentional, not a placeholder bug: `edit_form()`, called right after, already falls back to `$team->name`/a generated description for display when either is blank, and the row is only meant to become a real placeholder until the founder submits that form) and `0` for `rights` in `team_admins.php` (confirmed `rights` isn't actually read anywhere in this codebase or upstream's own `team_admins.php`/`team.inc`, so this has no behavioral effect beyond avoiding the crash).

Happy to open a PR for both.

title: Several small, independent bugs found while auditing stock BOINC PHP code
body:
Unrelated to each other, found while auditing a running BOINC project's own bug-fix history against current upstream:

- **`html/ops/manage_user.php`, `handle_suspend()`** — assigns `$admin->email_addr` without ever initializing `$admin`. PHP <8 silently auto-vivified this into a `stdClass`; PHP 8 throws "Attempt to assign property on null" instead — fatally, on every single suspend/unsuspend action, after the `forum_preferences` UPDATE has already committed but before either notification email goes out.
- **`html/ops/manage_user.php`, `possibly_delete_user()`** — calls `delete_user()` (`html/inc/user_util.inc`), but this file only `require_once`s `util.inc`/`user.inc`/`team.inc`/`forum.inc`/`util_ops.inc`/`profile.inc`/`project.inc` — none of which pull in `user_util.inc`. Every "Delete user" click fatals with "Call to undefined function delete_user()" before deleting anything.
- **`html/inc/profile.inc`, `scale_image()`** — `$destWidth`/`$destHeight` are computed via float division but passed straight into `ImageCreateTrueColor()`/`ImageCopyResampled()`/`ImageCreate()`/`ImageCopyResized()`, all of which take `int` parameters. Throws a PHP 8.1 "Implicit conversion from float to int loses precision" deprecation notice on every profile picture upload.
- **`html/ops/login_form.php`** — `strlen(sanitize_local_url(get_str('next_url', true)))`: `get_str(..., true)` returns `null` when the param is absent (the common case), and `strlen(null)` is deprecated as of PHP 8.1.
- **`html/ops/create_forums.php`, `create_category()`/`create_forum()`** — both have a "look up the existing row on insert failure" fallback meant to make the script safely re-runnable, but it's dead code: modern PHP/mysqli throws `mysqli_sql_exception` on a failed query by default instead of returning `false`, so a duplicate-key insert (what a second run produces, since both tables have unique keys) crashes with an uncaught exception before ever reaching the fallback.
- **`html/inc/util.inc`, `page_head()`** — two bugs in how it emits page metadata: (1) the `DARK_MODE` branch hardcodes 5 stylesheet hrefs (`sample_bootstrap.min.css`, `bootstrap_darkly.min.css`, `custom_dark.css`, `custom.css` ×2) as bare relative paths, unlike every other CSS/JS reference in the same function (`STYLESHEET`/`STYLESHEET2`/the non-dark-mode fallback all correctly prefix with `$url_base`) — breaks on any page generated below the site's top level. (2) The `SHORTCUT_ICON` tag hardcodes `type="image/x-icon"` regardless of the actual file type, and echoes the path unprefixed by `$url_base` (again unlike `STYLESHEET`/`STYLESHEET2` right above it) — risks the browser refusing a non-ICO file and 404s outside the top-level directory.
- **`unserialize(get_cached_data(...))` unguarded against `null`, PHP 8.1 deprecation, in 4 files**: `html/user/server_status.php`, `html/user/download_network.php`, `html/user/get_project_config.php`, `html/user/team_members.php`. `get_cached_data()` returns `null` on a cold/expired cache. `get_project_config.php` is the more consequential of the four — it's the scheduler's own `get_project_config` RPC response, so an unguarded notice there injects straight into the raw XML every BOINC client parses on attach, not just onto a web page.
- **`xml_parse($parser, $prefs_xml, 1)` unguarded against `null`, PHP 8.1 deprecation, in `html/inc/prefs.inc`'s `prefs_parse_global()` and `html/inc/prefs_project.inc`'s `prefs_parse_project()`** — `$user->global_prefs`/`$user->project_prefs` are nullable DB columns (null for anyone who's never saved custom preferences). Affects every caller that goes through these two functions (`prefs.php`, `add_venue.php`, `prefs_edit.php`, `prefs_remove.php`).

All confirmed present on current `master`. Happy to open PRs for these.

title: project.sample/: two bugs in the reference bootstrap template
body:
Two independent bugs found in `html/project.sample/`, the reference template every new BOINC project bootstraps from (via `make_project`):

- **`project_specific_prefs.inc`, `project_specific_prefs_parse()`** — checks `if (!$p)` after `simplexml_load_string()` to detect a parse failure:
  ```php
  $p = simplexml_load_string($prefs_xml);
  if (!$p) {
      error_page("Can't parse prefs:\n$prefs_xml\n");
  }
  ```
  A `SimpleXMLElement` with no child elements is falsy in PHP even when parsing succeeded — `simplexml_load_string()` only returns `false` on an actual parse failure. Since `COLOR_PREFS`/`GFX_CPU_PREFS` are both `false` in this same sample file, every user's project-specific prefs XML is legitimately just `<foo></foo>` — empty by design, not malformed. Any project starting from this sample unmodified hits "Can't parse prefs:" for every single visitor to their project-prefs page. Fix: check `=== false` instead of the falsy `!$p`.

- **`project.inc`** — `SYS_ADMIN_EMAIL`, `UOTD_ADMIN_EMAIL`, and `POST_REPORT_EMAILS` are built as `"admin@$master_url"`. `master_url` is a full URL (e.g. `https://example.org/myproject/`), not a bare domain, so these produce something like `admin@https://example.org/myproject/` — never a valid, deliverable address. Any project that doesn't know to override these three constants silently loses forum-abuse reports and other admin-notification emails. Suggested fix: derive a bare domain via `parse_url()` before building these, or at minimum comment that these must be overridden before going live.

Both confirmed present on current `master`, both reproduced against a real deployment before writing this up.

Happy to open PRs for both.

title: 6 confirmed translation bugs in html/languages/translations/it_IT.po
body:
Six confirmed bugs in the `it_IT` translation, found on a real deployed site and re-verified against the current source `.po` file just now. Two categories:

**Placeholder corruption** — BOINC's `tra()` substitution only matches the literal `%1`/`%2`/etc. token, so any corruption of that exact string shows through unsubstituted or garbled:

| `msgid` | Current (broken) `msgstr` | Bug |
|---|---|---|
| `Already joined? %1Log in%2.` | `Già effettuato l'accesso? 1%1Accedi %2.` | stray literal `1` typo'd in front of `%1` |
| `About %1` | `Informazioni su %s` | `%s` used instead of the `%1` convention — never substituted |
| `You can meet and communicate with other %1 participants...` | `...gli altri % 1 partecipanti...` | stray space *inside* the placeholder (`% 1` not `%1`) |
| `...At this point BOINC should be installed...%2get help here%3...` | `...Se no, 1%2ottieni aiuto qui%3...` | same stray-`1` typo, this time in front of `%2` |

**Plain translator typos** (not placeholder-related):

| `msgid` | Current (broken) `msgstr` | Bug |
|---|---|---|
| `...If you need help, %1go here%2.` | `...Se ti serve aiuto, %1go qui%2.` | English word "go" left untranslated instead of "vai" |
| `If BOINC is not installed on this computer, %1download it%2.` | `...puoi %1dscaricarlo da qui%2.` | "dscaricarlo" isn't a word — missing "s", should be "scaricarlo" |

Suggested corrected `msgstr` values:
- `Già effettuato l'accesso? %1Accedi%2.`
- `Informazioni su %1`
- `Puoi incontrare e comunicare con gli altri %1 partecipanti\n        in diversi modi: dai un'occhiata menu\n        Community qui sopra.`
- `\n    Ora BOINC dovrebbe essere installato e operativo nel tuo computer;\n    l'icona nella system tray dovrebbe essere simile a: %1\n    Se no, %2ottieni aiuto qui%3.\n    `
- `Il tuo computer non ha ancora completato nessuna attività.  Se ti serve aiuto, %1vai qui%2.`
- `Se BOINC non è installato su questo computer puoi %1scaricarlo da qui%2.`

Since translations go through Transifex rather than a GitHub PR, I'll submit these corrected strings there directly (`explore.transifex.com/boinc/boinc/`) — filing this issue too so it's tracked here as well, and so anyone hitting the same strings in the meantime can find the fix.

title: lib: Guard get_mem_info() definition for Linux
body: Wrap the `get_mem_info()` definition in procinfo_unix.cpp with an `ifdef __linux__` preprocessor guard to match its declaration in `procinfo.h`. Assisted-by: ChatGPT: GPT-5.6 Luna Fixes an unreported non-Linux build error in procinfo_unix.cpp. **Description of the Change** The `PROCINFO::get_mem_info()` declaration in `procinfo.h` is guarded by `#ifdef __linux__`, but the corresponding definition in `procinfo_unix.cpp` is not. On FreeBSD, this causes the compiler to encounter an out-of-line definition for a member function that is not declared in `PROCINFO`: `error: out-of-line definition of 'get_mem_info' does not match any declaration in 'PROCINFO'` Guard the definition with the same `#ifdef __linux__` condition used by the declaration. This keeps the existing Linux behavior unchanged while allowing the source to compile on FreeBSD. The Linux-only declaration was added in commit 2743c05. **Alternate Designs** One alternative is to remove the `#ifdef __linux__` from the declaration in `procinfo.h` and provide implementations for other Unix platforms. That would unnecessarily broaden the scope of this change, since `get_mem_info()` currently reads Linux `/proc//status` data and the reported problem is that the function is being defined on platforms where it is not declared. Another alternative is to change the FreeBSD implementation to provide an equivalent `get_mem_info()` function. That is also outside the scope of this change. The proposed change keeps the existing platform-specific design and makes the definition match its existing declaration. **Release Notes** N/A --- ## Summary by cubic Wraps the `get_mem_info()` and `get_field()` definitions in `procinfo_unix.cpp` with an `#ifdef __linux__` guard to match their declarations in `procinfo.h`. This fixes a FreeBSD build error where the out-of-line definitions didn't match any declaration; Linux behavior is unchanged. Written for commit d988b1892bf8e775fce455303159c43585456172. Summary will update on new commits.

title: team_import.php: don't let one team's failure kill the whole run
body: Addresses #4779's team_import.php crash. `handle_team()`'s per-team loop had no try/catch around it at all, so any uncaught exception during processing — a duplicate-key collision, an encoding issue like the one in #4779, or anything else a single team's data can trigger — kills the entire run mid-list. Every team after the failing one silently never gets processed, and since most collisions/data issues recur identically on every subsequent run, the import can get stuck at the exact same point forever. Confirmed independently via a different trigger: two real official teams whose placeholder founder both had the display name "Coordinador" hit `user.name`'s unique constraint, throwing the same uncaught `mysqli_sql_exception` shown in #4779's own stack trace. Fix wraps each team's `handle_team()` call in try/catch so one team's failure becomes an isolated, logged skip instead of a total outage — every other team still gets processed. Tested against a deliberately crafted collision fixture: the unpatched script reproduces the exact crash-and-stop behavior; the patched version logs the failure and continues to the next team. Note this only covers the try/catch — `delete_spammers.php`'s separate `strftime()` deprecation reported in the same issue is untouched, happy to look at that too if useful. --- *Assisted by AI (Claude Sonnet 5) per the BOINC AI Assistants Usage Policy — see the commit's `Assisted-by:` trailer.* --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes `team_import.php` so one team's import failure no longer kills the whole run — each team is processed in a try/catch, failures are logged and skipped, and the script exits non-zero if any team failed. - Converts the hard `exit()` calls in `update_team()` and `insert_case()` into thrown exceptions so the per-team try/catch catches them instead of terminating the script. - Covers the duplicate-`user.name` crash from #4779. - `delete_spammers.php`'s `strftime()` deprecation is not addressed here. Written for commit 544398ac161809df5eddeb9f50b36d3a38c12a59. Summary will update on new commits.

title: create_forums.php: catch the duplicate-key exception so the fallback runs

title: guard unserialize(get_cached_data()) against a cold cache in 4 files
body: Addresses one of the bugs reported in #7296. `get_cached_data()` returns `null` on a cold/expired cache, and 4 files pass that straight into `unserialize()` unguarded — a PHP 8.1 deprecation notice ('Passing null to parameter #1 ($data) of type string is deprecated'). A `SimpleXMLElement` with no child elements is falsy in PHP even when parsing succeeded — `simplexml_load_string()` only returns `false` on an actual parse failure. Since `COLOR_PREFS`/`GFX_CPU_PREFS` are both `false` in this same sample file, every user's project-specific prefs XML is legitimately just `` — empty by design, not malformed. title: send_forum_notification_email() references undefined $thread instead of $forum — fatal on PHP 8+
body:
`html/inc/forum_email.inc`'s `send_forum_notification_email($forum, $user)`:
```php
function send_forum_notification_email($forum, $user){
    $title = PROJECT . ": there is a new thread in '". $forum->title ."'";
    $link = secure_url_base() . "forum_forum.php?id=" . $forum->id;
    $body = "A " . PROJECT . " user has added a thread to the forum
\"" . $thread->title . "\".\n"
```
$thread isn't in scope in this function at all — only $forum and $user are parameters (the $title line two lines above correctly uses $forum->title). Under PHP 8+, $thread->title on an undefined (and therefore null) variable is a **fatal error** ("Attempt to read property 'title' on null"), not just a deprecation notice — this function crashes every time it's actually called.

Same class of bug as the $action/$action_name issue fixed in #7292 — likely a copy-paste artifact from the very similar send_thread_notification_email() right above it, which does correctly use $thread.

Confirmed present on current master, and genuinely reachable through ordinary user action: forum.inc's own create_thread() (called whenever a user starts a new thread, e.g. forum_post.php) calls notify_forum_subscribers(), which calls notify_forum_subscriber() for each subscriber with pm_notification=1 — so this crashes for real the moment someone posts a new thread in a forum that has at least one such subscriber.

Fix: $thread->title → $forum->title.

Happy to open a PR for this.

---
