title: Banishment vote outcome is never enforced — intentional (advisory only) or a gap?
body:
Tracing through `html/inc/forum_banishment_vote.inc` and its two callers (`forum_banishment_vote.php`, `forum_banishment_vote_action.php`), I want to check whether this is the intended design or an incomplete implementation:

- **Starting a vote (`start_vote()`) immediately suspends the accused user for exactly 6 hours** (`banished_until = time() + 21600`), before a single vote is cast. That same 6-hour window is also the vote's own deadline (`vote_is_in_progress()` checks `end_time > now`).
- **The notification email tells the accused they'll be banned for 14 days if the vote succeeds** (`send_banish_vote_email()` is called with `86400*14` as the duration), but I can't find anywhere that this 14-day figure — or the vote's tally at all — is ever actually applied. `vote_yes()`/`vote_no()` just record a row and re-print the current tally; nothing checks for a majority, nothing extends `banished_until` based on the result, and I couldn't find any cron task or other code path that revisits a vote after its 6-hour window closes.

So as far as I can tell, the practical effect of a banishment vote is entirely the automatic 6-hour suspension that fires the moment it's *started* — the vote itself (and the 14-day figure promised in the email) appears to be advisory only, with no automated follow-through. A moderator would have to separately notice the outcome and use the unrelated direct "Banish author" tool if they want an actual longer ban.

Confirmed present on current `master`. Is this the intended behavior (vote as a soft signal + built-in cooldown, real enforcement left to human judgment), or is there meant to be a mechanism that acts on the tally after the vote closes that's missing/broken? Happy to look into a fix once there's clarity on the intended design.

---

*This report (investigation) was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Sonnet 5). All findings were verified against the actual BOINC source.*

title: Proposal: shared email_greeting()/email_footer() helpers for consistent plain-text emails
body:
## Summary

Stock `html/inc/email.inc` and the various `send_*_email()` functions across the codebase have no
shared header/footer, and the result is inconsistent from one email to the next. Some examples from
the current code:

- `send_auth_email()` ends with a "For further information and assistance with PROJECT, visit ..."
  block.
- `send_thread_notification_email()`/`send_forum_notification_email()` end with a different
  "--------------------------\nTo change email preferences, visit:\n...\nDo not reply to this
  message." block.
- `send_moderation_email()`, `send_thread_moderation_email()`, `send_banish_email()`,
  `send_banish_vote_email()` have **no footer at all** — the message just stops.
- None of them open with any kind of greeting.

On our own project (Camicia) we put together a small shared pair of helpers to fix this:

```php
function email_greeting($user) {
    return "Hi $user->name,\n";
}

function email_footer($prefs_link = true) {
    $footer = "\n--\n".PROJECT."\n".secure_url_base()."\n";
    if ($prefs_link) {
        $footer .= "\nTo change your email preferences, visit:\n"
            .secure_url_base()."edit_forum_preferences_form.php"
            ."\nDo not reply to this message.\n";
    }
    return $footer;
}
```

`email_greeting()` for the opening line (only used for emails going to a real named recipient, not
role-addressed ones like `POST_REPORT_EMAILS`), and `email_footer($prefs_link)` for the closing
block — `$prefs_link` gated because emails to project/team admins aren't gated by *their* forum
notification preferences, so it doesn't make sense to point them at that page.

Applied across `email.inc`, `forum_email.inc`, `friend.inc`, `pm.inc`, `uotd.inc`, `ops/notify.php`,
`ops/manage_user.php`, `ops/team_import.php`, and `user/team_founder_transfer_action.php` — every
`send_*_email()` we could find. Along the way this also surfaced two real bugs already reported/fixed
separately (#7311/#7312, and a dead-code duplicate `$subject` assignment in
`send_thread_moderation_email()`).

## Question for maintainers

Is this worth contributing back, and if so, at what scope? A few things in what we did are more a
matter of taste than a fix, and we'd rather ask first than send a big diff that assumes the answer:

1. **The helpers + consistent usage** (the part above) seems like a plain improvement regardless of
   project — happy to open a PR for just this if it's wanted.
2. We also changed subject lines from `"[PROJECT] x"` to `"PROJECT: x"` for consistency — purely
   cosmetic, easy to drop if you'd rather keep the brackets.
3. For emails that currently go to *both* a named user and an admin/moderator list with the same
   body (e.g. `send_banish_email()`, `send_moderation_email()`), we split them into a personal
   greeting+footer version for the user and a separate third-person version for admins. This is more
   than styling — it changes what admins actually see — so it may be worth its own separate
   discussion regardless of whether 1) is wanted.

Happy to open PR(s) for whichever of these make sense, scoped however's easiest to review.

---
*Drafted with AI assistance (Claude, Anthropic) per the project's AI Assistants Usage Policy.*

title: db_purge: batch a workunit's result deletions into one "where id in (...)" query
body: ### What `db_purge` deleted each of a workunit's results with its own `delete from result where id = X` query in `purge_and_archive_results()`. For a project with `target_nresults = N` that's `N` round-trips per workunit on top of the one for the workunit itself. This collects the result IDs while archiving and issues a single `delete from result where id in (id1, id2, ...)` per workunit instead. The `IN ()` list is chunked at 1000 IDs so the generated query stays well within `MAX_QUERY_LEN` (262144) — 1000 twenty-digit IDs plus separators is ~21 KB. Partly addresses #6735 — workunit and assignment deletes are still one-per-row; batching those defers deletes across a whole `do_pass()` and widens the archived-but-not-deleted window much further, so I left it for a separate change. ### Unchanged - **Archiving** — still per-result, same order, same `archive_result()` / `archive_result_gz()` paths. - **`--dont_delete`** — still logs `Didn't purge result [...]` per result and deletes nothing (the ID list stays empty). - **Per-result logging** — `Purged result [id] batch N` is still emitted for every purged result (now grouped after the batched delete rather than interleaved with individual deletes). - **PR #5694's invariant** — a workunit is still never deleted unless its results all deleted first: a failed batch delete returns the error, `do_pass()` does `continue`, and the workunit + results are retried next pass. - **`--max`, `--max_wu_per_file`, `enable_assignment`, the workunit delete itself, `number_results`** — untouched. ### Behaviour change Result deletes are issued once per workunit, after the workunit has been fully archived, instead of one immediately after each result is archived. If `db_purge` is killed (OOM / power loss) between archiving a workunit's results and the batched delete committing, the restart re-enumerates the workunit and re-archives its entire result set — previously this window was at most one result. No DB inconsistency (the workunit is still never deleted while any of its results survive) and archive entries are keyed by ID for de-duplication, but it's a real change to crash-recovery behaviour in the area #5694 touched. Also: the two `DB_RESULT` deletes previously happened while a `mysql_store_result`-buffered enumeration over `result` was open; they now happen after that enumeration finishes, which is strictly safer. ### Testing - `g++ -fsyntax-only` against the real headers is clean, no new `-Wall -Wextra` warnings. - The chunking of `delete_ids_from_db()` was unit-tested in isolation: 0 IDs -> 0 queries, 3 -> 1, exactly 1000 -> 1, 1001 -> 2, 2500 -> 3; no leading/trailing commas; full-width IDs format correctly. - I couldn't run a full server build in my environment; relying on CI for the complete compile/link. --- *Assisted by Claude (Sonnet 5) per the [BOINC AI Assistants Usage Policy](https://github.com/BOINC/boinc/wiki/Contributing-to-BOINC-with-AI-assistants); the commit carries the `Assisted-by:` trailer. I've read the full diff and verified the behaviour described above.* --- ## Summary by cubic Batches result deletions in `db_purge` from one query per result to a single `WHERE id IN (...)` query per workunit, reducing database round-trips. The query is chunked at 1000 IDs to stay within `MAX_QUERY_LEN`. **Behavior change** - Result deletes now happen after the whole workunit is archived, so a crash in that window re-archives the entire result set on restart (previously at most one result). Archiving order, `--dont_delete` handling, and the per-result log format are unchanged. - Per-result purge logs are emitted after each chunk's delete commits, so a failure on a later chunk doesn't hide results already deleted. Written for commit 41a4f11b49d7635dc9b1c8b8385fbe561db579d0. Summary will update on new commits.

title: cache.inc: cache_check_diskspace() uses undefined constant USER_HOST_TTL (PHP 8 fatal)
body:
### Describe the bug

`html/inc/cache.inc`, in `cache_check_diskspace()`:

```php
$x = max(TEAM_PAGE_TTL, USER_PAGE_TTL, USER_HOST_TTL,
    USER_PROFILE_TTL, TOP_PAGES_TTL, INDEX_PAGE_TTL
);
```

`USER_HOST_TTL` is not defined anywhere in the tree — `git grep USER_HOST_TTL` returns only that one line. `html/project.sample/cache_parameters.inc` defines `TEAM_PAGE_TTL`, `USER_PAGE_TTL`, `USER_PROFILE_TTL`, `TOP_PAGES_TTL`, `INDEX_PAGE_TTL`, `STATUS_PAGE_TTL`, `REMOTE_PROJECTS_TTL` — but not `USER_HOST_TTL`. No caller passes it to `get_cached_data()` either; it looks like a cache category that was planned and never wired up.

On PHP 8 an undefined constant is a fatal `Error` (on PHP 7 it was an `E_WARNING` and evaluated to the string `"USER_HOST_TTL"`, which `max()` harmlessly ignored among the integers).

### Impact / reachability

`cache_check_diskspace()` returns early unless `rand() % CACHE_SIZE_CHECK_FREQ == 0` (default 1 in 1000) **and** `disk_usage("../cache") >= MAX_CACHE_USAGE` (default 10 MB). So this only affects a project on the **file** cache backend (not memcached) once its `html/cache/` dir grows past 10 MB — at which point roughly 1 request in 1000 returns HTTP 500 instead of pruning the cache. Narrow, but it's a live fatal and the pruning it was meant to do silently never happens.

### Suggested fix

Drop `USER_HOST_TTL` from the `max()` list — nothing uses that TTL, so `clean_cache()`'s age threshold is unchanged in practice. (Alternatively add it to `cache_parameters.inc`, or wrap it in `defined()`.)

Found while reviewing #6310; independent of that.

---
*Reported with AI assistance (Claude Sonnet 5); verified against `master` @ `b4b1bad96f`.*

title: cache.inc: BoincMemcache::get() rebuilds the Memcached connection and re-adds servers on every call
delete_job_files: inverted active-batch check deletes in-use job files and never reaps finished ones
body:
### Describe the bug

`html/ops/delete_job_files` reaps `job_file` rows (and their download-hierarchy files) once `delete_time` has passed. Per its own header comment — and `job_file.php`'s — it should delete a file only when it has **no associations to active batches**. The in-use check is inverted:

```php
// associations to batches in state INIT / IN_PROGRESS (still active)
$query = "select * from DB.batch_file_assoc as bfa join DB.batch
    where bfa.job_file_id=$file->id and bfa.batch_id=batch.id
    and batch.state < BATCH_STATE_COMPLETE";
...
$b = _mysql_fetch_object($result);
if (!$b) continue;        // no active-batch association -> skips deletion
...                       // active-batch association found -> deletes the file
```

`if (!$b) continue;` skips deletion when the file is **not** used by any active batch, and falls through to `unlink()` + `$file->delete()` when it **is**.

### Impact

- A `job_file` past its `delete_time` that's still referenced by an INIT/IN_PROGRESS batch has its input file deleted from `download/` while jobs still need it -> download failures / WU errors.
- A `job_file` whose batches are all COMPLETE/ABORTED/RETIRED is never reaped -> the file (these are the large shared input files remote submission is meant to support) leaks indefinitely.

The inverted condition has been present since the original 2013 Condor commit (`7f4263b07`); the 2017 "fix delete_job_files" (#1844) only corrected an unrelated `md5`->`name` reference. Blast radius is limited to projects that installed `db/schema_condor.sql` (so `batch_file_assoc` exists) and schedule this script themselves — it's in no stock `config.xml` task list.

### Suggested fix

`if (!$b) continue;` -> `if ($b) continue;` (an active-batch association should *prevent* deletion).

While here: `unlink($path)` leaves the `$path.md5` sidecar orphaned, and neither `unlink` return is checked.

Found while reviewing #6577 (which would build on this daemon).

---
*Reported with AI assistance (Claude Sonnet 5); verified against `master` @ `b4b1bad96f`.*

title: create_work rejects result template paths longer than 63 bytes despite allowing 256 chars.
body:
### Describe the bug

Although `create_work.cpp` initially stores the `--result_template` argument in a 256-byte buffer, that's only an input buffer. It then passes the value to `create_work2()`, where the filename is stored in the `DB_WORKUNIT::result_template_file` field which is only `char[64]`. The effective limit is therefore 63 bytes. The 256-byte front-end buffer does not make longer paths usable.

This limit is becoming restrictive for the CPDN project which we've had to work around several times.



### Steps to reproduce

For example, this path is 64 bytes:

`upload_templates/cpdn-jasmin-upload/result_template_oifs_n10.xml`

With the template file present, `create_work` fails with:

```
result template filename is too big: 64 bytes, max is 63
create_work: buffer overflow
```

In current master, `tools/backend_lib.cpp` checks:

`if (strlen(result_template_filename) > sizeof(wu.result_template_file)-1)`

The backing `DB_WORKUNIT::result_template_file` field is still `char[64]`, so only 63 bytes are accepted.

### Expected behavior

1. Path sizes should be consistent between front-end commands and back-end DB tables.
2. Increase DB table to allow for 128 character result template paths as 63 is restrictive.

title: boinc_zip can cause task fails during Windows Update activity
body:
### Describe the bug

**Summary**

CPDN has observed repeated failures in BOINC tasks related to Windows Update. Investigation of failures showed that around 5% of task fails on Windows occurred when Update was running. 

The failures were pinned down to when CPDN tasks were actively creating zip archives of task results through boinc_zip function calls. The correlation with Windows Update was sufficiently consistent that boinc_zip was identified as the point of failure.

There are a number of other issues with boinc_zip detailed below which suggest to me that BOINC should consider deprecating this code and leave projects themselves to decide how best to package input & results files, with the added benefit of reducing BOINC's technical debt.  

I am not aware of what other projects use boinc_zip but I no longer use boinc_zip for our recent models having introduced a modern C++ streams based library (ZipLib), which offers other compression algorithms. I believe CPDN was the original author of the boinc_zip code?

**Details**

The underlying boinc-zip code uses low-level C runtime and file APIs such as `fopen`, `fdopen`, `fileno`, `fstat` and `unlink`. Windows file descriptors are a C-runtime compatibility layer over native Windows HANDLE objects, and file access is also governed by Windows sharing modes.

BOINC already contains Windows-specific filesystem handling which retries transient failures and opens files with permissive sharing modes, for example [boinc_fopen()](https://github.com/BOINC/boinc/blob/master/lib/filesys.cpp#L580-L623). However, the legacy Info-ZIP paths used by boinc_zip appear to call the underlying C/Info-ZIP filesystem functions directly, bypassing these BOINC-specific retry and sharing mechanisms.

This is likely the explanation for the CPDN failures: a transient Windows Update file-sharing conflict may cause a low-level zip operation to fail immediately, without sufficient retrying or useful native Windows error information being reported.

This should not be interpreted that C-runtime file descriptors cannot be used on Windows. The concern is that the legacy implementation does not appear to handle Windows sharing semantics and transient file locks robustly when external system activity is accessing the same files.

**Additional concerns**

The boinc_zip library has other issues:

- uses fixed-size buffers
- unbounded string-copy operations
- leaks memory (Valgrind)

These are independent memory-safety issues, but they increase the risk of failures when processing long paths or filenames.

GPT was used for scanning code to help in diagnosing the problem and drafting the initial issue summary.


### Steps to reproduce

_No response_

### Expected behavior

**Requested investigation**

Personally I would suggest considering deprecating the boinc_zip library. If not, a number of changes need to be considered.  Please investigate whether boinc_zip should:

1. Retry transient Windows sharing and access failures.
2. Use BOINC’s Windows-aware filesystem helpers consistently.
3. Preserve and report the underlying Windows error code and filename.
4. Avoid assumptions based on Unix-style descriptor behaviour.
5. Be replaced or modernised using a Windows-compatible archive implementation.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### System information

Windows 10 & 11 only.

### Additional context

_No response_

title: Mac: Fixes to Xcode projects and build scripts for Xcode 27
body: Mac: always set deployment target to SDK's oldest supported MacOS version Xcode has always suggested a range of recent MacOS versions to target as the oldest MacOS your code will support (the _deployment target_.) The oldest suggested MacOS version has always increased with each successive version Xcode, but in the past one could enter a MacOS version older than any of the suggestions.. Xcode 27 now treats any deployment target older than its suggestions as a compilation error. For Xcode 27, the oldest OS support version is MacOS 12.0 Monterey introduced in October 2021. Since the minimum deployment target increases with each subsequent version of Xcode, entering a fixed value would normally require manually updating each project 's deployment target each time. To avoid that, I have implemented code which automatically determines the oldest version of MacOS supported by the current version of Xcode and dynamically sets the deployment target to that value. This is needed for all the Xcode projects, including the main BOINC project (client, Manager, installer, uninstaller, screensaver controller, default screensaver and BOINC libraries), VBoxWrapper, Docker Wrapper, UpperCase, Remove Podman and the boinc_zip wrapper for libzip. Corresponding changes must also be made to the various build scripts for building the dependent libraries and for the samples with Mac scripts for building using Makefiles (either in addition to or instead of an Xcode project): Uppercase, VBoxWrapper and Wrapper. Xcode 27 also requires updating wxWidgets to version 3.3.3. For several years, we have always set the deployment target to MacOS 10.13. This is no longer possible. Apple releases a new version of Xcode with each major version of MacOS, typically once a year. Unfortunately, this means that the oldest version of MacOS on which newer versions of BOINC can run will keep changing. **Release Notes** Fixes to Xcode projects and build scripts for Xcode 27 --- ## Summary by cubic Xcode 27 rejects builds whose deployment target is older than the SDK's minimum supported macOS, so Mac builds now derive the deployment target from the current SDK instead of a hardcoded 10.13. BOINC builds on new Xcodes, but its minimum supported macOS (currently 12.0) tracks the SDK and will rise with each Xcode release. **New Features** - New `mac_build/BOINC.xcconfig` holds the deployment target; each scheme's pre-build action regenerates it from `SDKSettings.plist` `MinimumDeploymentTarget`. - The same approach covers `boinc_zip`, `UpperCase2`, `vboxwrapper`, `docker_wrapper`, and RemovePodman, each with its own `.xcconfig`. - `BuildMacBOINC.sh` regenerates those files because `xcodebuild` ignores scheme pre-actions, and the generated `.xcconfig` files are untracked in git. - The pre-actions and `BuildMacBOINC.sh` abort the build if the deployment target can't be read from the SDK. - The dependent-library build scripts (`buildcurl.sh`, `buildopenssl.sh`, `buildfreetype.sh`, `buildWxMac.sh`, `buildFTGL.sh`, `buildc-ares.sh`, `buildlibzip.sh`) and the sample make-file scripts (`MakeMacExample.sh`, `BuildMacVboxWrapper.sh`, `BuildMacWrapper.sh`) derive the deployment target the same way; the library scripts force x86_64 builds as a temporary Xcode 27 workaround. - The example app's `Makefile_mac2` delegates deployment-target derivation to a new `Makefile_mac2_helper.sh`, and `buildMacMakefiles-CI.sh` now expects universal binaries from `MakeMacExample.sh`. - Fixes syntax and error-checking bugs in build scripts and removes a duplicate library check in `BuildMacBOINC.sh`. **Refactors** - Drops the hardcoded 10.13 target and related build settings (`-bind_at_load`, `PREBINDING`, `-DMAC_OS_X_VERSION_MAX_ALLOWED`); the screensaver XIB was updated to the Xcode 27 tool version. - The installer scripts build packages with `pkgbuild --ownership preserve` to fix ownership and permissions, including the branded installer's path handling; the notarization script switched from csh to sh, supports testing dev builds, and detects the built app's architecture from the BOINC Manager binary instead of assuming it. - Requires Xcode 15 or later for all updated build scripts and `BuildMacBOINC.sh`, wxWidgets 3.3.3, and curl 8.21.0. Written for commit a73c702210d4dc3609b0eb0c69f7e272f90bf3e9. Summary will update on new commits.

title: Don't ship the SysV init script in client packages
body:
Fixes #7272

## Description of the Change

All Linux package targets are systemd-only and ship `boinc-client.service`, but the client packages also installed the obsolete SysV script `/etc/init.d/boinc-client`. On openSUSE Leap 16, where the distribution removed `systemd-sysv-install` entirely, the presence of that script makes `systemctl enable` abort — so the RPM `%post` failed (zypper exit 107), the service was left disabled, and the client was dead after a reboot, exactly as reported.

As requested in the issue, the script is dropped from all client packages (RPM and DEB). It is removed at the deployment manifest, so it never enters the client payload that feeds either package:

1. **Manifest** (`deploy/prepare_deployment.py`): drop `./client/scripts/boinc-client` from `linux_client_list`. The script is no longer collected into the client archive, so neither the RPM nor the DEB ships it and no per-package `rm` is needed.
2. **RPM** (`rpmrepo/package_prepare.sh`, `rpmrepo/package_filelist.sh`): stop expecting the init script, and move the client `systemctl enable --now` from `%post` to `%posttrans`. The `%posttrans` move covers the upgrade path: `%post` runs before the old package's files are removed, so the init script from an already-installed affected package would still break the enable.
3. **DEB** (`debrepo/package_prepare.sh`, new `packages/deb/preinst` and `packages/deb/postrm`, updated `packages/deb/postinst`): stop shipping the init script, and clean up a copy left on disk by a previous package. BOINC's own `.deb` never declared it a conffile, but the distribution-maintained `boinc-client` packages (versioned `+dfsg`) do, and dpkg preserves obsolete conffiles across upgrades unless a maintainer script removes them. A `dpkg-maintscript-helper rm_conffile` call — in `preinst`, `postinst` and `postrm`, as the helper requires — removes it on that upgrade path. (Debian/Ubuntu were never broken, since they still provide `systemd-sysv-install`; on the `.deb` side this is cleanup.)
4. **Tests** (`tests/linux_package_integration_tests.py`): the two `/etc/init.d/boinc-client` assertions (existence and ownership) are replaced by an assertion that the script is absent, for all package targets.

## Testing

Packages for every target were built by replaying the workflow's packaging steps on the official payloads, then installed in containers running systemd as PID 1.

**RPM** (suse16_0, fc43, fc44): fresh install of the patched package leaves the service enabled and active, `boinccmd` responds, and no init script is present; the new integration-test assertion passes. Upgrade from the stock package removes the init script and the service stays enabled and active. On Leap 16 the stock package reproduces the report (enable fails, service left disabled), and the patched package installs cleanly with the service enabled.

**DEB** (jammy, noble, resolute, bookworm, trixie): fresh install of the patched package leaves the service enabled and active, `boinccmd` responds, and no init script is present. Upgrade from a BOINC repository package removes the script and the service stays up.

**DEB upgrade from a distribution `+dfsg` package**: because that package registers the init script as a conffile, this path is handled by the new maintainer scripts. It was verified with a focused `dpkg` test — installing a package that ships `/etc/init.d/boinc-client` as a conffile, then upgrading to a package carrying these scripts, removes the script; a locally-modified copy is preserved as `/etc/init.d/boinc-client.dpkg-bak` rather than deleted.

## Alternate Designs

- Making `%post` tolerate the sync failure would hide the install-time error but leave every later `systemctl enable`/`disable` cycle broken on Leap 16 — rejected in the issue discussion.

## Release Notes

Linux client packages no longer install the obsolete SysV init script `/etc/init.d/boinc-client`. On openSUSE Leap 16 the client service is now correctly enabled at install time and starts after a reboot. Upgrades from older packages that shipped the script remove it, including distribution packages that shipped it as a conffile.

---

This was worked on with AI assistance. I have reviewed and tested everything myself as well.

title: Remote submission: script access to batch output; job turnaround times in query_batch
body:
Fixes #7389 (problem and plan described there).

Scripts that use the remote job submission API can query and abort batches with the account authenticator, but cannot download the output of batch-collect batches (BUDA among them) or compute job turnaround, and `query_completed_job` fails for jobs that have no canonical instance.

**Changes**
- `get_output3.php` — `check_auth()` accepts `auth_str = md5(authenticator . batch_id)` instead of a login cookie, the scheme `get_output.php` already uses (`boinc_get_output_files_url()`). The value must be a string and is compared with `hash_equals`; a non-string `auth_str` (`auth_str[]=…`) fails with "bad auth_str". Requests without `auth_str` behave as before.
- `submit_rpc_handler.php`, `show_job_details()` — for the canonical instance, also `elapsed_time`, `sent_time`, `received_time` (only new XML elements; existing clients unaffected).
- `submit_rpc_handler.php`, `query_completed_job()` — used an undefined `$job_id` and could leave `$result` unset for a job with no canonical instance (on BOINC Central this request returns HTTP 500 for such jobs); now `$wu->id` and `$result = null`.

**Testing**
- `php -l` on both files.
- `check_auth()` exercised in a small PHP harness with `BoincBatch`/`BoincUser`/`get_str`/`error_page` stubbed: right `auth_str` → allowed; wrong one, one computed for another batch, an array, an empty `auth_str` or `auth_str=0`, unknown batch → refused; no `auth_str` → unchanged login path. (Harness in the PR thread on request.)
- Not run on a live BOINC server. The client side was tested against BOINC Central for the existing endpoints; the new `auth_str` path and the new XML fields need a server with this patch.

**AI assistance**: written with Claude Code; each commit carries an `Assisted-by:` trailer, per https://github.com/BOINC/boinc/wiki/Contributing-to-BOINC-with-AI-assistants.

title: Remote job submission: download batch output without a login cookie; job times in query_batch; query_completed_job fails for jobs without a canonical instance
body:
## Problem

Scripts that use the remote job submission API (`submit_rpc_handler.php`, e.g. via `lib/submit_api.py`) can query and abort batches with the account authenticator, but some things are only possible from a logged-in browser:

1. **Output of batch-collect batches (e.g. BUDA).** `get_output3.php?action=get_batch_tar|get_batch_zip` checks only the web login cookie (`get_logged_in_user()`), so a script cannot download a batch's output. The older `get_output.php` already supports `auth_str = md5(authenticator . batch_id)` for exactly this (`boinc_get_output_files_url()`).
2. **Job turnaround.** `query_batch` with `get_job_details` reports `cpu_time` of the canonical instance but not its `elapsed_time`, `sent_time`, `received_time`, so clients cannot compute what the web page shows as turnaround.
3. **`query_completed_job` for a job with no canonical instance** (all instances errored) uses an undefined `$job_id` in `BoincResult::enum("workunitid=$job_id")` and may leave `$result` unset; on BOINC Central this request returns HTTP 500, so a client cannot see the stderr of failed jobs.

## Proposed change

- `get_output3.php`: in `check_auth()`, if `auth_str` is given, look up the batch and its owner and accept the request iff `auth_str` is a string equal (`hash_equals`) to `md5(owner->authenticator . batch_id)`; otherwise behave as now. Same scheme as `get_output.php`, no new secret.
- `submit_rpc_handler.php`: in `show_job_details()`, add `elapsed_time`, `sent_time`, `received_time` next to `cpu_time` for the canonical instance (only new XML elements).
- `query_completed_job()`: use `$wu->id`, initialise `$result = null`.

Use case: a client for agents/scripts that follows BUDA batches on BOINC Central (https://github.com/ispacex/boinc-central-mcp). A PR implementing this is #7387.

title: Bug Report: Incorrect Disk Space Detection in Boinc 8.2.11 for Windows
body:
### Describe the bug

There is a serious bug in Boinc version 8.2.11 for Windows. When a disk is approximately 70–75% full or more, the application incorrectly reports that no storage space is available, regardless of the storage settings.

Example:
If a 500 GB drive has 400 GB of used space, there should be approximately 100 GB of free space remaining. However, Boinc reports 0 MB available, preventing any further downloads.

This issue affects all projects, not just a specific one.

Additionally, uninstalling and reinstalling the application, along with other basic troubleshooting steps, does not resolve the issue.

Expected behavior: Boinc should correctly detect the available disk space and allow downloads as long as sufficient storage is available.

Actual behavior: Boinc incorrectly reports 0 MB of available storage, blocking downloads even when significant free space remains.

This appears to be a storage detection or disk space calculation issue in the Windows version of Boinc 8.2.11.

This behavior persists even after changing the storage usage preferences in the BOINC settings and on the project website; in other words, no matter what value you enter, the same error continues to occur.

An example from an event log: 

19.10.2026 19:16:36 | LHC@home | Sunucudan mesaj: Theory Simulation needs 7629.39MB more disk space.  You currently have 0.00 MB available and it needs 7629.39 MB.

title: [client] Check rootless Podman user and group ID mappings
body: Fixes #6867. ## Description of the change Linux and WSL check rootless Podman's UID and GID mappings before accepting it for BOINC. A shared parser requires coverage of container IDs 1..65536 in both maps, including configurations split across multiple host ranges. Gaps and overlaps cannot inflate the available coverage. Explicit `rootless: false` accepts rootful operation with empty mappings. The WSL probe uses the same user-selection policy as task execution: older boinc-buda-runner distros use the default user; other supported distros run tasks as root. The distro version is read before detection. A successful mapping diagnosis requires both completed pipe reading and a zero process exit code; command/parse failures are not reported as missing sub-IDs. WSL setup, launch and command failures are logged as inability to verify mappings; they do not disable Podman. The info probe uses private pipes so delayed output cannot reach subsequent probes. An unfinished process is asked to terminate, with a bounded wait and a diagnostic if stopping it cannot be confirmed. Process and pipe handles are closed. Configuration guidance tells users to check `/etc/subuid` and `/etc/subgid` and allocate non-overlapping ranges for the BOINC user, followed by `podman system migrate` as the BOINC user, rather than prescribing a potentially occupied range. ## Validation - Eight GTests using the project's class and `TEST_F` convention passed against the production parser and MIOFILE, covering single/split ranges, ordering, gaps, overlaps, boundaries, missing maps, rootful mode and unrecognized output. The test is included by the existing CMake discovery and registered as `ClCompile` in the Windows unit-test project. Its filter entry follows the existing `ClInclude` convention, as [requested in review](https://github.com/BOINC/boinc/pull/7399#discussion_r4430273482). - Thirty-four external parser/WSL fixture cases passed, including eleven focused lifecycle cases for successful/failed launches, exit-status failures, timeouts, termination races, pipe isolation and failure diagnostics. The original code fails the pipe-isolation regression. Windows process/pipe APIs are stubbed in those fixtures; no new test infrastructure is added to this PR. - Repository source-code/trailing-whitespace checks, project XML parsing and `git diff --check` passed. Native Windows/WSL execution and end-to-end Podman workloads were not tested locally. Hosted checks are tracked separately. ## AI assistance Codex assisted with implementation review, validation and preparation of this description. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #6867 by validating rootless Podman on Linux and WSL against `podman info`, requiring user and group subordinate ID mappings that cover IDs 1..65536. When mappings are missing, Podman is marked unavailable and a configuration hint is shown. An explicit `rootless: false` bypasses the check, so rootful Podman with empty mappings continues to work. - In WSL, the check only runs when a distro runs Podman as its default user (boinc-buda-runner below version 4), matching `setup_podman`; the distro version is therefore read before Podman detection. - The parser accepts split or non-contiguous host ranges as long as they cover the required container IDs, and fails separately on command errors versus missing mappings. - WSL probes that time out or die are terminated with a bounded wait and their handles closed so they cannot interfere with later commands; the `read_from_pipe` EOF status and process exit code are verified. - WSL setup, launch, and command failures log an inability to verify mappings and leave Podman enabled. - Adds parser GTests covering split ranges, gaps, overlaps, boundaries, missing maps, rootful mode, and unrecognized output; registered in the Windows unit-test project. title: [android] Promote Monitor to foreground before asynchronous setup
body: Fixes #7244. ## Description of the change On Android O and later, `Monitor.onStartCommand` publishes the foreground notification before mutex acquisition and asynchronous client setup. Startup therefore does not depend on a later status update meeting the foreground-service deadline. Notification transitions are serialized; mutex/setup failure stops foreground mode. Regular status updates decide whether computing remains in the foreground. When suspension notifications are enabled, leaving foreground retains the notification using the API-appropriate detach operation; otherwise it removes it. Changes to `active` rebuild the notification even when ClientStatus is unchanged, keeping priority correct during screen-off updates and reactivation. ## Validation The complete `ClientNotificationTest` class passed: 104 tests. These cover notification state/priority changes, retained versus removed notifications and API-specific foreground calls. Four focused service-start tests passed (two scenarios on API 26 and 28), using the actual Monitor service and ClientNotification. They verify notification publication before mutex acquisition, failure followed by another start, and repeated starts without duplicate periodic scheduling. Only timer scheduling and the mutex/RPC boundary are mocked; native client setup and scheduled status updates are not exercised by these tests. Tests use the repository Gradle/AGP configuration in an isolated SDK environment. The relevant production/test files match the submitted source. Repository source-code/trailing-whitespace checks and `git diff --check` passed. No physical-device or emulator end-to-end run was performed. ## AI assistance Codex assisted with implementation review, validation and preparation of this description. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes the Android O+ foreground-service startup timeout by calling `startForeground()` before mutex acquisition and asynchronous client setup in `Monitor.onStartCommand`, so the startup deadline can't be exceeded. - Previously the foreground notification was only set during the async status update, which could exceed the startup deadline and crash with `ForegroundServiceDidNotStartInTimeException`. - Notification updates and foreground transitions are now serialized; foreground mode is stopped when mutex acquisition or client setup fails. - If the mutex is already held when the service restarts, the foreground state is refreshed immediately. - The notification is now refreshed when only the active state changes (e.g. screen-off updates), with its priority updated accordingly. - When leaving foreground, the notification is detached rather than removed if `showNotificationDuringSuspend` is enabled, and removed otherwise. - New `MonitorLifecycleTest` cases cover failed mutex acquisition stopping foreground, retry on a later start, and repeated starts refreshing foreground without extra periodic tasks. title: [server] Repair expired job-file cleanup and retain retryable failures
body: Fixes #7319. ## Description of the change Restore the missing job-file enumeration and association-deletion helpers and correct the inverted active-batch guard. Expired input files are retained while any associated batch is INIT or IN_PROGRESS (`state < BATCH_STATE_COMPLETE`). Cleanup, queries/renewal and uploads share database-scoped filename locks. Cleanup rechecks row identity, TTL and batch associations after locking; busy files are retried on a later pass. Database deletion is transactional and checked. Filesystem failures retain metadata, including for sidecar retries; filesystem unlinks cannot be rolled back. Uploads reuse retained metadata, preserve associations and never shorten a TTL. Repeated associations are idempotent. Filename lookup preserves spaces and `"0"`, follows the existing unique index's collation and explicitly rejects conflicting physical spellings. RPC lock/query failures return escaped XML errors. Cleanup now computes paths without creating directories. It checks directory access and requires an observed file/sidecar to be successfully unlinked. Rollback and unlock failures are handled independently so unlock is still attempted; recovery failure stops the process with an error instead of reusing an uncertain connection. ## Storage assumptions Existing automatic cleanup of missing files is retained; no new operator option is introduced. Directory accessibility cannot prove that the intended storage volume is mounted. If an unavailable volume leaves an accessible empty hierarchy behind, this PR does not distinguish that from an already absent file. Deployments must ensure the intended download storage is available before scheduling cleanup; mount-health policy is outside this fix. ## Validation Sixty-four behavioral cases passed in an isolated PHP/MariaDB environment using the production schema, constraints, cleanup script and full RPC endpoint. Coverage includes batch states, exact filenames/collation, renewal and association races, concurrent upload/query/cleanup, retained-row retries, sidecars, broken symlinks, missing directories, storage disappearance after file observation, and rollback/unlock failures in strict and non-strict mysqli modes. Authentication and unrelated web setup are fixtures; no production database or download directory is used. The comprehensive harness remains outside the source tree. PHP syntax, repository source-code/trailing-whitespace checks and `git diff --check` passed. Hosted CI and maintainer review are tracked separately. ## AI assistance Codex assisted with implementation review, validation and preparation of this description. --- ## Summary by cubic Repairs expired job-file cleanup in `html/ops/delete_job_files`, keeping files while any associated batch has not reached `BATCH_STATE_COMPLETE`. - Adds per-file database locks shared with `html/user/job_file.php` so cleanup no longer races uploads, queries, or TTL renewal. - Cleanup builds the download path directly and verifies the directory, so it no longer creates directories on an unavailable mount. - Cleanup rechecks the current unique row and all batch states after locking; busy or replaced files are skipped for the next run. - Deletes the file, its `.md5` sidecar, and database records in a transaction; any failed deletion keeps the records for the next run. - `job_file.php` takes the same locks, only creates a batch association when none exists, refuses case-distinct filenames that collide, and leaves metadata for cleanup retries. title: win_build: parallel PostBuildEvent race in example_app_atiopencl and example_app_nvopencl copying openclapp_kernels.cl
body:
### Describe the bug

In parallel MSBuild builds (`win_build/boinc.slnx`), `example_app_atiopencl.vcxproj` and `example_app_nvopencl.vcxproj` have identical project dependencies (`libboinc`, `libboincapi`, `libboincopencl`) and both define the same `PostBuildEvent` writing to the shared `$(OUTDIR)`:

- https://github.com/BOINC/boinc/blob/4d1529df3b47fffa3a903dc3632e10e983e069bc/win_build/example_app_atiopencl.vcxproj#L23-L25
- https://github.com/BOINC/boinc/blob/4d1529df3b47fffa3a903dc3632e10e983e069bc/win_build/example_app_nvopencl.vcxproj#L23-L25

```xml
<PostBuildEvent>
  <Command>copy ..\samples\openclapp\*.cl "$(OUTDIR)"</Command>
</PostBuildEvent>
```

When both projects finish linking at the same instant, both execute `copy ..\samples\openclapp\*.cl "$(OUTDIR)"` concurrently targeting `$(OUTDIR)\openclapp_kernels.cl`. One of the two `copy` processes fails with a Windows file-sharing violation (`The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process`), failing the entire MSBuild job with `error MSB3073`.

### Evidence from GitHub Actions (`Debug-x64-msbuild`)

Observed in job https://github.com/BOINC/boinc/actions/runs/40974122309/job/123797830055:

```text
2026-10-30T00:40:23.5287201Z     54>PostBuildEvent:
2026-10-30T00:40:23.5288188Z          copy ..\samples\openclapp\*.cl "D:\a\boinc\boinc\win_build\Build\x64\Debug\"
2026-10-30T00:40:23.5288985Z          :VCEnd
...
2026-10-30T00:40:23.5476480Z     54>PostBuildEvent:
2026-10-30T00:40:23.5479019Z          ..\samples\openclapp\openclapp_kernels.cl
2026-10-30T00:40:23.5479810Z     55>PostBuildEvent:
2026-10-30T00:40:23.5480309Z          ..\samples\openclapp\openclapp_kernels.cl
2026-10-30T00:40:23.5492623Z     54>PostBuildEvent:
2026-10-30T00:40:23.5493332Z                  1 file(s) copied.
2026-10-30T00:40:23.5494113Z     55>PostBuildEvent:
2026-10-30T00:40:23.5494798Z          The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process.
2026-10-30T00:40:23.5496247Z                  0 file(s) copied.
2026-10-30T00:40:23.5553011Z     55>C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\18\Enterprise\MSBuild\Microsoft\VC\v180\Microsoft.CppCommon.targets(166,5): error MSB3073: The command "copy ..\samples\openclapp\*.cl "D:\a\boinc\boinc\win_build\Build\x64\Debug\" [D:\a\boinc\boinc\win_build\example_app_nvopencl.vcxproj]
```

### Possible fix

Remove the shell `copy` `<PostBuildEvent>` and copy the kernels with an explicit MSBuild `<Copy>` task, keeping the existing `<None>` item so the file stays visible in Solution Explorer:

```xml
<Target Name="CopyOpenCLAppKernels" AfterTargets="Build">
  <Copy SourceFiles="..\samples\openclapp\openclapp_kernels.cl" DestinationFolder="$(OutDir)" SkipUnchangedFiles="true" Retries="10" RetryDelayMilliseconds="500" />
</Target>
```

`SkipUnchangedFiles` alone does not help here: on a clean parallel build the destination does not exist yet for either project, so both copies still run. The actual mitigation is the documented `Retries`/`RetryDelayMilliseconds` parameters of the `Copy` task, which ride out the momentary sharing violation.

The kernel is named explicitly rather than with a `*.cl` wildcard, so a renamed or deleted kernel fails the build: `Copy` logs `Copy.SourceFileNotFound` as an error, while an empty wildcard would silently copy nothing. `samples/openclapp` has a single kernel and `openclapp.cpp` loads that single file name, so there is nothing to gain from a wildcard.

A `<CopyFileToFolders>` item (the Visual Studio "Copy File" item type) would also work, but it is undocumented for desktop C++ projects and relies on an implicit destination folder; the explicit `Copy` task makes the retry policy and the source file visible in the project file.

---

Reported with AI assistance; findings and CI log evidence verified against `master` @ `4d1529df3b`.

title: [win_build] Copy the OpenCL sample kernel once per build
body:
Fixes #7408. Supersedes #7409.

## Description of the change

The two OpenCL examples used shell copy events that could concurrently write `openclapp_kernels.cl` to the same output directory and fail with a Windows sharing violation.

Both examples now invoke `CopyOpenCLAppKernels` in the shared child project `win_build/openclapp_kernels.proj`, forwarding `OutDir`. MSBuild shares the target result for the same child project and global properties within one build invocation. Either example can still be built independently; solution dependencies and `None` items remain unchanged.

The explicitly named kernel is copied unconditionally once per shared project instance. Missing source and copy errors fail the build, and same-size/same-timestamp stale output is refreshed. There are no retries or warning suppressions. Separate MSBuild processes or differing global-property sets targeting the same destination are not coordinated.

## Validation

The standalone fixture and workflow test step were removed as requested in review. Ten fixtures run outside the source tree passed with .NET SDK 10.0.403 MSBuild on Linux, covering independent/concurrent callers, solution scheduling, output isolation, missing source, stale/deleted output and propagated failures. title: server: maintain batch stats on the fly; speed up batch list display
body:
Keep track of batch stats (# of done, error, in-progress jobs) on the fly, so that when we display lists of batches
we don't have to enumerate the (possibly 10000s) of jobs in each batch.

Add the following DB fields:
```
workunit.n_sent: how many instances have been sent batch.n_success: # of success jobs
batch.n_in_progress: # of WUs with:
    wu.canonical result == 0
    wu.error mask == 0
    wu.n_sent > 0
```
Logic changes:
```
scheduler, when send a result for WU:
    if wu.n_sent == 0:
        batch.n_in_progress++
    wu.n_sent++
    Note: race conditions may cause batch.n_in_progress to be too big.
    Don't worry about this.

validator, when get canonical instance:
    batch.n_in_progress--
    batch.n_success++

transitioner, when set wu.error_mask for first time
    batch.nerror_jobs++
    if wu.n_sent > 0
        batch.n_in_progress--
```

title: [sched] Detect cycles and bound zombie host chain traversal
body: ## Summary `authenticate_user()` in `sched/handle_request.cpp` could loop indefinitely if zombie host records form a cycle. This change detects cycles and bounds the number of links followed. ## Root cause When hosts are merged on the web (`merge_hosts()` in `html/inc/host.inc`), the old host becomes a "zombie": its `userid` is set to 0 and `rpc_seqno` holds the ID of the host it was merged into. When a client sends a zombie's host ID, the scheduler follows these links: ```cpp retval = host.lookup_id(g_request->hostid); while (!retval && host.userid==0) { // TODO: check for infinite loop retval = host.lookup_id(host.rpc_seqno); ... } ``` If two zombie host records cross-reference each other (or one references itself), the scheduler loops until CGI timeout while issuing a DB lookup on every iteration. ## Fix - Track visited host IDs in a small fixed array up to `MAX_ZOMBIE_HOST_LINKS` (16). - Stop immediately if `host.rpc_seqno <= 0`, if the next ID matches the current host or any previously visited host in the chain, or if `MAX_ZOMBIE_HOST_LINKS` is reached. - Log a `MSG_CRITICAL` diagnostic when an invalid target (`rpc_seqno <= 0`), cycle, or excessive chain length is detected, set `retval = ERR_DB_NOT_FOUND`, reset `g_reply->hostid = 0`, and fall through to the existing broken zombie chain handling (which creates a new host record). - Remove the `TODO` comment. Fixes #2433 --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes scheduler stalls when zombie host records form cycles. `authenticate_user()` follows links from merged host records (`userid=0`, `rpc_seqno` → target host), but a self-reference or a cross-reference between two zombies made it loop indefinitely, issuing a DB lookup on every iteration until the CGI timed out. - Tracks visited host IDs up to `MAX_ZOMBIE_HOST_LINKS` (16); stops on self-links, cycles, non-positive target IDs, or the hop limit. - Logs an `MSG_CRITICAL` diagnostic for broken chains and falls through to the existing handling that creates a new host record. Fixes #2433. Written for commit c4e1bc760932e3c18558fd1a1e5b284b9fb22f93. Summary will update on new commits.

title: [android] Ask for the project's account identifier
body:
## Summary

The project attach screens always asked for `Email address:`, `Name:` and `Password:`, whatever the project uses as account identifier. Projects identify accounts by email address unless their `get_project_config` reply sets `uses_username`, in which case they identify accounts by user name (matching the desktop BOINC Manager).

## Change

The Manager now asks only for the account identifier that the selected projects use:

- Email-based project (`uses_username` is false): `Email address:` + `Password:`.
- User-name-based project (`uses_username` is true): `User name:` + `Password:`.
- Batch selection containing both types of projects: `Email address:` + `User name:` + `Password:`.

Details:

- New `CredentialInputs` helper computes the needed fields and minimum password length from the `ProjectConfig`s (`emailAddress = !login || configs.any { !it.usesName }`, `userName = configs.any { it.usesName }`, `minPwdLength`).
- `CredentialInputActivity` (batch input) waits until the project configs are retrieved, then hides the field that none of the selected projects need and enables the Continue button.
- `IndividualCredentialInputFragment` shows only the identifier field needed for that project. If the user clicks `Register` on a username-based project while the email address field is hidden, the dialog first reveals and focuses the email address field without submitting prematurely; the dialog is only dismissed once `onFinish()` confirms that input validation (`CredentialInputs.findError()`) succeeded and attachment started.
- `ProjectAttachService.verifyInput()` only requires the fields that are needed for the selected project(s) and validates password length against `minPwdLength`.
- When creating an account on an email-based project without a separate user name input, `CredentialInputs.defaultUserName()` derives a valid BOINC user name (satisfying server-side `is_valid_user_name()`) from the local part of the email address, stripping special characters and prefixing `user_` if the local part is numeric (e.g. `123456@example.com` -> `user_123456`).
- `attachproject_login_header_id_name` changed from `Name:` to `User name:` in `values` and `values-en` (required by `validate_android_translations.py`). Other translations are not modified.
- `uses_username` was already parsed into `ProjectConfig.usesName`, so the parser does not change.

## Testing

- New unit tests: `CredentialInputsTest` (unknown config, email-based, user-name-based login & registration, mixed projects, `defaultUserName` sanitization/numeric handling, and `findError` validation including `minPwdLength`).
- `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest assembleRelease` passes.
- `python ci_tools/validate_android_translations.py` passes, and so does `git diff --check`.

Fixes #5389

title: samples/nvcuda: support Linux arm64 cross-compilation
body: ## Summary Currently, the `samples/nvcuda` sample application (`example_app_nvcuda`) is only built in Linux CI for native `x86_64` (`apps` and `apps-vcpkg`), and is not cross-compiled for Linux `arm64` (`apps-arm64` and `apps-vcpkg-arm64`). ## Change Enable cross-compilation of `samples/nvcuda/example_app_nvcuda` for Linux `arm64` (`aarch64`) using the NVIDIA CUDA SBSA cross-compilation toolkit: - **`.github/workflows/linux.yml`**: - Run the host CUDA toolkit installation step (`cuda-toolkit-${{ env.CUDA_VERSION_MM }}`) for `apps-arm64` and `apps-vcpkg-arm64` in addition to `apps` and `apps-vcpkg` so `/usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc` and host build tools are available. - Add an `Install CUDA for apps-arm64 and apps-vcpkg-arm64` step that installs `cuda-repo-cross-sbsa-$distro_name-${{ env.CUDA_VERSION_MM }}-local_${{ env.CUDA_VERSION_MMP }}-1_all.deb` and `cuda-cross-sbsa-${{ env.CUDA_VERSION_MM }}` (which populates `/usr/local/cuda/targets/sbsa-linux/{include,lib}`). - **`m4/cuda.m4` & `samples/Makefile.am`**: - Select `$cuda_root/targets/sbsa-linux` (or `$cuda_root/targets/aarch64-linux`) as the target CUDA directory when `$host_cpu` is `aarch64` or `arm64`, and choose `lib64` or `lib` accordingly. - Verify that `-lcudart` links (`AC_CHECK_LIB([cudart], [cudaMalloc], ...)`) in addition to checking `cuda_runtime.h`, determine `CUDA_CCBIN` (falling back to `${CUDA_CCBIN##* }` if `CXX` contains a compiler wrapper such as `ccache`), substitute `CUDA_CCBIN` via `AC_SUBST`, and export it in `samples/Makefile.am`. - **`samples/nvcuda/Makefile`**: - Detect `arm64`/`aarch64` cross-compilation via `RELEASE_ARCH`, `TARGET_ARCH`, or `aarch64` in `CXX`, and set `CUDA_INCLUDE_PATH` and `CUDA_LIB_PATH` to `$(CUDA_INSTALL_PATH)/targets/sbsa-linux/{include,lib}` (or `targets/aarch64-linux`). - Pass `-ccbin "$(CUDA_CCBIN)"` (defaulting `CUDA_CCBIN ?= $(CXX)` for standalone invokes) and the target include/library directories to `$(CUDA_NVCC)` when compiling `cuda_kernel.cu`. - Add an explicit `cuda.o: cuda.cpp` rule so GNU Make's built-in `.cpp.o` rule does not pass `$(TARGET_ARCH)` as a compiler flag if `TARGET_ARCH` is set in the environment. ## Testing - Cross-compiled `samples/nvcuda/example_app_nvcuda` on Linux `x86_64` targeting `aarch64-linux-gnu` (`./configure --host=aarch64-linux ...` with `CXX=aarch64-linux-gnu-g++` and CUDA 13.3 + `cuda-cross-sbsa-13-3`): - Verified `configure` detects CUDA 13.3, `cuda_runtime.h`, `-lcudart`, and `nvcc -ccbin aarch64-linux-gnu-g++`. - Verified `samples/nvcuda/example_app_nvcuda` is built as an `ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable, ARM aarch64` linked against `libcudart.so.13`. - Built `samples/nvcuda/example_app_nvcuda` natively on Linux `x86_64` with CUDA 13.3 and verified the resulting `x86-64` ELF executable. Fixes #7162 --- ## Summary by cubic Enables cross-compiling `samples/nvcuda/example_app_nvcuda` for Linux arm64 (aarch64) using the NVIDIA CUDA SBSA cross-compilation toolkit. - Installs `cuda-toolkit` and `cuda-cross-sbsa` in the Linux CI workflow for the `apps-arm64` and `apps-vcpkg-arm64` jobs. - Updates `m4/cuda.m4` to select `targets/sbsa-linux` (or `targets/aarch64-linux`) CUDA directories when cross-compiling for arm64, verifies `-lcudart` links for the target, and checks `nvcc` works with `-ccbin $CXX`. - Exports `CUDA_CCBIN` from `samples/Makefile.am` so the sample Makefile picks up the host compiler. - Updates `samples/nvcuda/Makefile` to pass `-ccbin "$(CUDA_CCBIN)"` to `nvcc` and use target-specific CUDA include and library paths for arm64. Fixes #7162 Written for commit d5ff8871a50c150b36db075722480b4008c91763. Summary will update on new commits.

title: [sched] Limit zombie host chain traversal to 10 hops
body: **Description of the Change** Per @davidpanderson's feedback in #7418, simplify the zombie host chain protection in `authenticate_user()` (`sched/handle_request.cpp`) to a simple loop counter (`++n > 10`) that exits with `ERR_DB_NOT_FOUND` and falls back to creating a new host record. **Release Notes** N/A Fixes #2433 Assisted-by: Antigravity:Gemini-4-Argon --- ## Summary by cubic Prevents infinite loops in `authenticate_user()` when following zombie host chain links by capping traversal at 10 hops, and clears the reply host id in the fallback path. Fixes #2433. - Exits the zombie chain loop with `ERR_DB_NOT_FOUND` after 10 hops so cyclic chains create a new host record instead of looping forever. - Resets `g_reply->hostid` to 0 when falling back to a new host, matching the existing `g_request->hostid` reset. ### Describe the bug **Description** In html/user/workunit.php, the job-results table is opened using: `result_table_start(false, true, null);` This calls start_table(), which opens both a \
wrapper and a \. However, workunit.php closes it using only: `echo "\n";` The enclosing \ remains open, causing subsequent content to be nested incorrectly. **Affected version** Confirmed in current master, commit 61056bd13bc2bd54eeb5f62b970eaf0bf5f07bed: - [Incomplete closure in workunit.php, line 119](https://github.com/BOINC/boinc/blob/61056bd13bc2bd54eeb5f62b970eaf0bf5f07bed/html/user/workunit.php#L119) - [Wrapper opened by start_table_str()](https://github.com/BOINC/boinc/blob/61056bd13bc2bd54eeb5f62b970eaf0bf5f07bed/html/inc/util.inc#L438) **Observed behaviour** On CPDN, the project header/footer hooks wrap the main content in a width-limited \, with the footer intended to sit outside it. The missing table-wrapper closure causes the footer hook’s closing \ to close the table wrapper instead. Consequently, the footer remains inside the restricted-width content area. The visible effect depends on the project’s layout, but the unbalanced markup exists independently of CPDN’s styling. ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Expected behavior Both the table and its wrapper should be closed before rendering subsequent content. **Proposed fix** Replace the manual closure after the results loop: ``` - echo "\n"; + end_table(); ``` **Verification** Replacing the manual closure with end_table() on CPDN’s live server restored the intended footer nesting and full-width appearance. title: Work fetch stops for multi-app projects when one app's max_concurrent is small (mc_max_could_use uses project-wide min MC)
body:
### Describe the problem

**Summary**
When any app of a project has `max_concurrent` in app_config.xml, the client estimates the project's maximum CPU usage as `project_min_mc × x`, where `x` is the largest `avg_ncpus` of any of the project's app versions (`RSC_PROJECT_WORK_FETCH::rr_init()` in `client/work_fetch.cpp`). For a project with several apps, one app with a low cap limits work fetch for the whole project, even when the other apps are uncapped or have much higher caps. The "MC shortfall" then becomes 0, and the project isn't chosen for fetch while most CPUs sit idle.

**Setup**
- 128-thread host, `max_ncpus_pct` 98 (125 usable CPUs), work buffer 0.25 + 0.03 days
- LHC@home with three CPU apps:
  - ATLAS (native_mt, avg_ncpus 3, max_concurrent 27)
  - CMS (vbox, 4 CPUs, max_concurrent 8)
  - Theory (1 CPU, no max_concurrent)
- Running: 4 Theory + 16 ATLAS + 8 CMS = 84 of 125 CPUs

**Observed** (work_fetch_debug)
```
[work_fetch] shortfall 2162372.40 nidle 89.00 saturated 0.00 busy 0.00
[LHC@home] [work_fetch] REC 145694.675 prio -1.003 can request work
[LHC@home] [work_fetch] share 1.000
[LHC@home] rsc type 0 last MC limit time 14401.36 total buf 24192.00
[LHC@home] can fetch CPU
[work_fetch] No project chosen for work fetch
```
A user-requested update logs `Not requesting tasks: don't need (CPU: ; ...)`, with no reason given.

`mc_max_could_use = min(8 × 4, 125) = 32`. With more than 32 CPUs in use, `mc_update_stats()` adds nothing, `mc_shortfall` stays 0, and `choose_project()` skips the project ("project has max_concurrent and has no shortfall"). Raising the ATLAS cap made no difference. Setting the CMS cap to 999 made the smallest cap 27, so 27 × 4 = 108, and fetch resumed immediately. A 24-CPU host with CMS capped at 3 is limited to 3 × 4 = 12 CPUs in the same way.


### Describe the solution you'd like

**Expected**
An uncapped app (Theory here) can use any free CPU, so the project's possible usage should be all usable instances. A low cap on one app should only limit that app's share.

**Suggested fix**
In `rr_init()`, compute `mc_max_could_use` per app instead of from the project-wide minimum:
- for each app with a version that uses this resource:
  - if the app has no `max_concurrent`: the project could use all instances → `mc_max_could_use = ninstances`, stop
  - otherwise: add `max_concurrent × (largest usage of that app's versions on this resource)`
- then apply `project_max_concurrent × x` if set, and cap at `ninstances`

The existing comment in `rr_init()` already notes that the estimate "doesn't take into account e.g. that the MC limit could be from a different app than the one that determined x".

**Workaround**
Don't use `max_concurrent` on the low-count app. That leaves no client-side way to limit it for projects that have removed their server-side per-host limits.

### Additional context

**Client version:** 8.2.13 (Linux); the same code is in 8.2.15 and master

title: [Manager] Prevent Manager crash on Windows 10 when switching Windows Light/Dark Themes
body: Fixes #7456 **Description of the Change** On Windows, changing the Windows theme kills the Manager with `0xC0000005`, with no crash report and no event-log entry. It is not a dark-mode bug: 8.3.0 dropped the `SUPPORTDARKMODE` guard that compiled this path out on Windows, so the handler re-creates the whole UI, and since one theme change is announced several times the second rebuild destroys the views the first one just created — `DeleteAllPages()` faults. Four changes in `clientgui`: - a burst of notifications collapses into **one** rebuild, deferred with `CallAfter`, so windows are not destroyed inside the message Windows is still dispatching; - the rebuild is decided by comparing the appearance in force with the one the last rebuild applied, instead of a flag cleared at the end — a switch is announced over a longer span than the rebuild takes, so the last notification used to arrive afterwards and start a second rebuild; - the appearance is read the way `BOINCGUIApp::OnInit()` reads it, `IsDark() || AreAppsDark()`, because `IsDark()` only reflects wxWidgets' own opt-in and lags the setting; - the chrome a switch leaves behind (DWM title bar, separator and padding above the notebook, status bar) is re-created rather than repainted. The rebuild itself is unchanged: it is what makes BOINC's colours follow the system setting, and it is still needed on macOS. **Alternate Designs** - *Defer the per-notification rebuild without coalescing.* Still two rebuilds per switch, with the echo re-entering the handler. - *Keep the flag and clear it later.* Tried: the notification span exceeds the rebuild, so the flag is already down when the last one arrives. - *Restore `SUPPORTDARKMODE` on Windows.* Drops Windows dark mode, and the crash is independent of it — a build with both dark-mode paths removed still crashes. **Release Notes** Windows: the Manager no longer crashes when the Windows theme changes, and its title bar, separator and status bar now follow the theme. **Testing** Windows 10 Pro 22H2, wxWidgets 3.3.3, same machine and data directory: | Build | Dark mode (wx / BOINC) | First theme switch | |---|---|---| | master, as shipped | on / on | crash, `0xC0000005` | | wx dark mode removed | off / on | crash | | both dark-mode paths removed | off / off | crash | | this branch | on / on | survives | - Survives repeated switches in both directions, colours following each time; 200 instrumented switches (50 launches, four flips each) plus 160 on the installed-form build: 0 deaths, one rebuild per switch. - Six switch captures compared band by band against a Manager started fresh in the same theme: every band matches. **AI assistance** Prepared with AI assistance (Mistral Vibe:DeepSeek V4.1 Flash); every AI-assisted commit carries an `Assisted-by:` trailer. I read the complete diff, the change matches the issue and its agreed approach, I reviewed it for correctness and security, I reproduced the crash and verified the fix by running the Manager as described above, and I can contribute it under BOINC's licensing and copyright terms (LGPL v3+, contribution assigned to The Regents of the University of California). I take responsibility for the change and for the review discussion. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes the Manager crash on Windows 10 when the Windows theme changes, with macOS and Linux behaviour unchanged. A single theme change is announced several times; the rebuild is now coalesced into one deferred rebuild per change and decided by comparing the appearance in force with the one last applied, so echo notifications can't start a second rebuild. The theme-change work — coalescing, the settle timer, the re-created DWM title bar, notebook panel, status bar and menus, the dialog colour fixes, and the simple view's labels and progress bar — is compiled only for MSW. Off Windows, the frames' rebuild runs once per notification exactly as it did before. - Collapses a burst of notifications into one deferred rebuild; a settle timer catches changes announced before the new appearance takes effect. - Reads dark mode via the shared `IsDarkAppearanceNow()` (`IsDark() || AreAppsDark()`), since `IsDark()` lags the setting. - Re-creates chrome a switch leaves behind — DWM title bar, separator, notebook padding, status bar, menu popups — and gives bare dialog panels and wizard pages an explicit background instead of Windows' `COLOR_APPWORKSPACE`. - Frees the accelerator table `CreateMenus()` replaces on a theme change in both frames, checking for null before deleting. - Links `dwmapi.lib` and `uxtheme.lib` through `boincmgr.vcxproj` and `configure.ac`, so MSVC and MinGW builds link too. Written for commit e407467122de1b8a3e677d4387b560af42bda309. Summary will update on new commits.

title: server: add sticky file support using DB; generalize BUDA input files
body: Also tweak client to include sticky flag in sched request. If an input file is 'sticky', it remains on the client even if not used by any WUs. This requires a mechanism for eventually deleting a sticky file (on clients) when it's not going to be used for any more jobs. Current server mechanisms for sticky files are inadequate. Stickiness is specified in input templates, which is not ideal. The scheduler tells clients to delete sticky files if their names match one of a list of regular expressions. This is far from ideal. With this PR, the list of currently active sticky files is kept in a DB table. The scheduler tells the client to delete a sticky file if it's not in this table. Sticky files are linked to batches (in another DB table). A sticky file can be 'released' if it's not linked to an active batch. In this case its DB record is deleted, so it will be deleted from clients after they do a scheduler RPC. This is integrated with BUDA (or similar batch submission system) as follows. The batch description file (.zip) can, instead of directly containing an input file 'foo', contain a file 'foo.toml' that describes this input file (which must be in the user's sandbox). This TOML file specifies the sandbox name; it can also specify - that the file is sticky - that the file is served from a remote URL (e.g. a CDN). Note: stickiness is no longer hardwired in the input template; it's specified on a per-batch, possibly per-job basis. You can have test batches without stick files, then use stickiness in production. This involves the following changes: - add DB tables (sticky_file and sticky_file_ref) and C++ and PHP interfaces - add update function to ops/db_update.php - add logic to BUDA submission to parse TOML files, and handle sticky and/or remote files. Since sticky files can be used by multiple batches, their physical names are jf_ rather than batch__ - add options to create_work to handle sticky and/or remote files - add web interface (user/sticky.php) - scheduler: skip regex-based deletion if no regex file if in config, do DB-based deletion --- ## Summary by cubic Adds DB-backed sticky file management, replacing regex-based client file deletion, and lets BUDA batch files reference input files via TOML descriptors. Sticky files are now tracked in DB tables and linked to batches. The scheduler tells clients to delete any sticky file not in the active table, and users can release files through a new web interface once their batches retire. BUDA batch zips can now contain `.toml` files that describe input files from the user's sandbox, optionally marking them sticky and/or fetchable from a remote URL. Stickiness is now set per batch or job rather than in the input template, and clients report the sticky flag to the scheduler. The scheduler reads the active sticky file list on each request, so it never deletes a file that was just added. **Migration** - Run `db_update.php` (version 27036) to create the `sticky_file` and `sticky_file_ref` tables. - Set `` in the scheduler config to use DB-based file deletion. title: scheduler: use format() to avoid possible buffer overruns
body: Anything that comes from scheduler request messages has to be treated with suspicion; GPU names or WSL distro names could be unboundedly long. Either use snprintf() and check the return value, or use strings and fmt::format --- ## Summary by cubic Replaces `sprintf`-based buffer formatting with `fmt::format` in the scheduler so unboundedly long GPU names and WSL distro names from request messages can no longer overflow fixed-size buffers. Adds `-lfmt` to the scheduler and test build flags. `host_info_json()` and `COPROCS::summary_string_json()` now return `std::string` instead of writing into caller-provided buffers, with `summary_string_json()` moved into the scheduler. `modify_host_struct()` now checks the JSON length before copying into `host.misc`, storing `"overflow"` if it would not fit instead of corrupting memory. Written for commit 338a935ca12481f0a00bbdf7682bdfa2296caf78. Summary will update on new commits.
